content.content:
# ReachyKit

Transport + domain core. No UI imports (SwiftUI/UIKit forbidden here). Swift 6 strict concurrency.

- `openapi.json` + `openapi-generator-config.yaml` → client generated at build time by the OpenAPIGenerator plugin
  (types + client, idiomatic naming). Refresh spec: `./bin/mise run update-spec` (fetches + normalizes null-type
  anyOf branches the generator can't handle — see `Scripts/normalize-openapi.py`).
- Pydantic `Optional[X]` without a default is _required and nullable_; the normalizer must also drop such properties
  from `required`, or the generated Swift field is non-Optional and a real null throws (`DaemonStatus.backend_status`).
- WebSocket endpoints are hand-written (not in the spec) — see `Transport/`.
- Unknown JSON fields must never break decoding (daemon updates independently of this app).
- `RobotAPIClient` supplies throwing defaults for everything except `handshake`, `daemonStatus`, `wakeUp` and
  `gotoSleep` — every test double must implement those four. `/wifi/*` and `/update/*` live on separate protocols so
  doubles for the connection surface stay small.
- Bluetooth layers as `BLETransport` (CoreBluetooth behind a seam; `FakeBLETransport` is the only stand-in, since the
  robot's GATT service is Linux/BlueZ) → `BLECommandPump` (one command at a time, write→read→maybe-notify) →
  `BLELink` (`@MainActor @Observable`, the screens' state). One link per transport: the response characteristic
  carries no correlation id, so a second pump on the same transport would race the first for its replies. Provisioning
  and recovery are therefore two halves of `BLELink`, not two session types (`BLELink+Recovery.swift`).
- Provisioning is written against `WiFiProvisioningTransport`, not against BLE: `BLEProvisioningTransport` and
  `RobotConnection` both implement it, so the sealing and the screens are shared and the HTTP path is available if the
  ~260-byte sealed payload turns out not to fit one ATT write. `WiFiConfigClient` adds the settings-only routes.
- `BLECommand` is the whole set the robot answers — anything else comes back as `ECHO:`. Renaming is **not** in it:
  daemon 1.9.0's dispatch has no `SET_NAME` branch, so a rename only works over HTTP.

# Daemon API knowledge

Base: `http://<host>:8000/api`. Port is configurable in our client (upstream hardcodes 8000).

## Spec

- REST: OpenAPI 3.1 at `Sources/ReachyKit/openapi.json`; canonical source
  `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pollen-robotics/reachy_mini/main/docs/source/API/openapi.json` (main is ahead of
  develop there). Refresh with `./bin/mise run update-spec` — it also normalizes `anyOf: [X, {type: null}]` branches
  that swift-openapi-generator silently drops (`Scripts/normalize-openapi.py`). Swagger UI at `http://<host>:8000/docs`
  when a daemon runs.
- WebSockets are NOT in the spec (FastAPI omits them). Known endpoints (from
  `reachy_mini/src/reachy_mini/daemon/app/routers/`):
  - `/api/state/ws/full` — full robot state (primary; take everything from here, REST `state/*` is fallback).
    Accepts query parameters that the spec cannot show. Defaults, read off `routers/state.py`:
    `frequency=10.0` (NOT 20 — and since the handler sleeps *after* building each frame, the real rate is a little
    lower), `with_head_pose=true`, `with_body_yaw=true`, `with_antenna_positions=true`, everything else false,
    including `with_head_joints` and `use_pose_matrix`. Modelled in `StateStreamOptions`.
    - **Never send `with_target_*`.** The frame builder asserts on them and the loop's blanket `except` swallows it,
      so the socket stays open and delivers nothing ever again. The only outward sign is a deduplicated
      `Skipping full-state frame:` line in the daemon journal. `StateStreamOptions` cannot express these on purpose.
  - `/api/move/ws/set_target` — live teleop
  - `/api/move/ws/updates`, `/api/move/ws/raw/write`
  - `/logs/ws/daemon` — daemon journal (NOTE: mounted at app root, not under `/api`, and ONLY with
    `--wireless-version` — absent on the simulator, upgrade rejected with 403)
  - `/api/apps/ws/apps-manager/{job_id}` — install/remove job stream (prefer over polling `job-status`)

## Wireless-only routes

- `/wifi/*` and `/update/*` mount at the app ROOT (no `/api`) and only under `--wireless-version`. The committed spec
  is generated without that flag, so they are absent from it and the generated client cannot reach them — hand-write
  them. A Lite robot 404s; gate on `DaemonStatus.wireless_version`.
- `/update/ws/logs` sends each line as a text frame AND then a `JobInfo` JSON frame repeating those same lines —
  decode JSON first and ignore its `logs`, or every line doubles. The job ends with `systemctl restart`, which kills
  the daemon before a terminal `done`: the socket closing is completion, confirmed by reconnecting and comparing
  versions. `available_version: "unknown"` means the ROBOT could not reach PyPI, not that the check failed.
- The daemon's own source is installed at `.venv-sim/lib/python3.12/site-packages/reachy_mini/` — read
  `daemon/app/routers/*.py` and `daemon/app/services/bluetooth/` there rather than guessing a shape. It is a
  specification (project rule 1), never code to port.
- `/wifi/*` routes, from `routers/wifi_config.py`: `GET /wifi/prov_key`, **`POST`** `/wifi/scan_and_list` (a POST
  because it rescans first; uncapped, unlike the 180-byte BLE reply), `POST /wifi/connect_sealed`,
  `GET /wifi/status`, `GET /wifi/error`, `POST /wifi/reset_error`, `POST /wifi/forget?ssid=`, `POST /wifi/forget_all`.
  Plaintext `POST /wifi/connect?ssid=&password=` exists and must never be called — the PSK would go in a query string.
- `connect_sealed` answers `400 decrypt_failed` for a wrong PIN **and** for a `kid` older than the 600 s rotation, and
  409 while another `nmcli` operation runs. It returns immediately and joins on a background thread; on failure it
  removes the connection and re-raises its own hotspot, so the reason ends up in `GET /wifi/error`, not in the reply.
- `GET /wifi/status` is `{mode: hotspot|wlan|disconnected|busy, known_networks, connected_network}` — a joined station
  is `wlan`, not `connected`, and there is **no IP address in it**. The BLE status characteristic is the mirror image:
  live address, no network names. Neither contains the other.
- `POST /wifi/forget` answers 404 for a network the robot never saved and 400 for `Hotspot`. Everywhere else in
  `/wifi/*` and `/update/*` a 404 means the route was never mounted, i.e. a Lite robot.
- `GET /api/daemon/hardware-id` answers one key, `{"hardware_id": "<16 hex>"}` = `sha256(usb serial)[:16]` — the same
  string as mDNS TXT `unit_id` and BLE characteristic `…cdef7`. It is a join key: never reshape it.

## Bluetooth service

Read `services/bluetooth/bluetooth_service.py` in `.venv-sim` — the dispatch table is one `if/elif` chain and settles
most questions in a glance.

- It is **its own systemd unit** (`reachy-mini-bluetooth`, working directory `/bluetooth`), not part of the daemon.
  Every recovery script ends with `systemctl restart reachy-mini-daemon`, so the Bluetooth link survives all of them —
  including `SOFTWARE_RESET`, which erases `/venvs` while the service sits outside it. `PING` therefore proves the
  robot is there, never that a reset finished.
- The commands are exactly `PING`, `STATUS`, `JOURNAL_{START,READ,STOP}`, `PIN_*`, `UPDATE_{CHECK,START,INFO}`,
  `WIFI_{KEYEX,STATUS,SCAN,CONNECT_ENC,FORGET}`, `CMD_*`. Anything else falls through to `ECHO:`. **There is no
  `SET_NAME`** — renaming is `POST /api/daemon/robot-name` and needs the robot on a network.
- The PIN is the last five characters of the Pollen audio device's USB serial (`38fb:1001`, read from
  `/sys/bus/usb/devices/*/serial`), compared verbatim: not necessarily digits, never case-folded. Do not uppercase the
  input field. Upstream states that serial is printed on the robot — it is **not** a separate code, and no route
  exposes it, which is the point. With no audio board attached the daemon falls back to a fixed `46879`.
- `CMD_*` clears the robot's own auth flag in a `finally`, so the PIN is needed again after every script — whether it
  succeeded or not. Its handler also returns `None` on success, so the reply encoder crashes and the GATT write
  reports an error for a script that ran perfectly.
- `_read_journal` returns `buffer[:480]` and **deletes what it returned**. One BLE read carries ~182 bytes, so the
  remainder of every large chunk is lost for good, and a line is regularly cut in half — `BLEJournalReader` carries the
  tail. The LAN journal is the authoritative one; say so in any UI that shows this.
  - The journal is a byte stream, not a message, so `BLEResponseParser` returns `.payload` **verbatim**. Trimming it
    (as every other reply is trimmed) eats the trailing newline that says the last line is complete, and the reader
    then glues that line onto the next chunk — one corrupted line per read boundary, which looks like nothing at all
    when a chunk holds a single line.
  - `journalctl` exits on its own; the GLib watch removes itself on HUP and every later read answers
    `ERROR: Journal not running`. That is a `JOURNAL_START` away from fixed, not a terminal state.
- `…cdef6` is `", ".join(...)` over the robot's `commands/` directory with `.sh` stripped, `"None"` when empty, in
  `os.listdir` order. Read it; never hardcode the list, and sort it before showing it.

## MVP endpoint subset (what upstream actually calls)

`daemon/status|start|stop`, `daemon/hardware-id`, `daemon/robot-name`, `state/full`, `move/set_target`,
`move/play/wake_up`, `move/play/goto_sleep`, `move/play/recorded-move-dataset/{dataset}/{move}`,
`move/recorded-move-datasets/list/{dataset}`, `motors/set_mode/{mode}`, `apps/job-status/{id}`, `kinematics/info`.

## Timeouts (from upstream `src/config/daemon.ts` — battle-tested values)

- Healthcheck request timeout: 2 s (3.5 s over Wi-Fi); status poll every 3 s (5 s Wi-Fi).
- Connected-state hysteresis: require 2 consecutive successful probes to go "connected"; downgrade immediately on
  failure.
- Job polling: 500 ms; app install timeout 60 s, remove 90 s, start 120 s; stale-job 90 s.

## Facts

- Daemon process ≠ robot backend. `/api/daemon/status` answers 200 with `backend_status: null` while the backend is
  torn down (`daemon.stop()` sets `self.backend = None`); every route behind the `get_backend` dependency
  (`move/*`, `state/*` incl. `ws/full`, `motors/*`, `kinematics/*`, `volume/*`) answers **503 "Backend not running"**.
  `camera/*` uses `get_daemon` instead, and `/logs/ws/daemon` is mounted at the app root — both outside that gate.
- Wake/sleep are multi-step protocols, not single calls: `motors/set_mode/enabled` → 300 ms → `move/play/wake_up`;
  sleep reverses it (animation first, `set_mode/disabled` only after it finishes). The play routes never touch the
  motor mode — an asleep robot accepts them, plays the sound, and does not move.
- `daemon/start?wake_up=<bool>` returns a job id immediately and starts the backend in the background (409 while
  another job runs); poll `daemon/status` until `running`. With `wake_up=true` the daemon enables the motors itself.
- No MJPEG endpoint exists. Camera is WebRTC-only (signaling `ws://<host>:8443`, GStreamer webrtcsink, single H.264
  Constrained Baseline 3.1 stream, Opus audio, STUN `stun.l.google.com:19302`).
- Daemon 1.9.0 is the minimum and tested API baseline. Enforce
  `DaemonCompatibilityPolicy` during the first status handshake: reject older/different-major versions, warn for
  newer 1.x or unknown versions, and tolerate unknown JSON fields. See `docs/adr/0001-daemon-compatibility-and-lan-security.md`.
- The daemon has no authentication or encryption. v1 supports trusted private LAN/robot AP only; never imply that a
  client-side token adds security and never expose port 8000 publicly.
- 9 actuators: `body_rotation`, `stewart_1..6`, `left_antenna`, `right_antenna`. Safety limits are clamped server-side.
- `passive_joints` in the state stream is `null` unless the daemon was launched with `--kinematics-engine Placo`; the
  default `AnalyticalKinematics` never computes them and there is no API to switch engines. The 21 Stewart passive
  joints are therefore worked out client-side, for 3D visualization only. Upstream's `kinematics-wasm` crate describes
  the behavior to reproduce — read it as a specification, never as code to port.
- URDF + STL meshes are served by the daemon: `GET /api/kinematics/urdf` (a `{"urdf": "<xml>"}` object, ~250 KB) and
  `GET /api/kinematics/stl/{filename}` (raw bytes as `model/stl` — its docstring claiming to return a *path* is
  stale). The generated client cannot fetch the STL: it declares `application/json` for every response.
- `GET /api/kinematics/info` reports only `{"info": {"engine", "collision check"}}` — no joint names, no limits. Those
  live in the URDF alone.
- DoA angle (microphone direction of arrival) is in radians: 0 = left, π/2 = front/back, π = right.
- Speaker and microphone levels are `GET|POST /api/volume/{current,set}` and `/api/volume/microphone/{current,set}`,
  both `{"volume": 0…100}` in and `{volume, platform, device}` out. There is no separate "sensitivity" concept —
  microphone sensitivity *is* its input level. Wrapped as `AudioLevel`.
  - **`POST /api/volume/set` plays a test sound on every accepted call** (it is in the route's own description).
    Send it once a slider gesture ends, never on each change, or the robot beeps continuously.
  - Out-of-range values come back as 422, so both setters map `.unprocessableContent` explicitly.
  - On `sim-daemon` these routes drive the **host Mac's own** speaker and mic (`platform: Darwin`), not a robot.
    Note the level before testing and restore it after.

  - `/api/move/ws/updates`, `/api/move/ws/raw/write`
  - `/logs/ws/daemon` — daemon journal (NOTE: mounted at app root, not under `/api`, and ONLY with
    `--wireless-version` — absent on the simulator, upgrade rejected with 403)
  - `/api/apps/ws/apps-manager/{job_id}` — install/remove job stream (prefer over polling `job-status`)

## Wireless-only routes

- `/wifi/*` and `/update/*` mount at the app ROOT (no `/api`) and only under `--wireless-version`. The committed spec
  is generated without that flag, so they are absent from it and the generated client cannot reach them — hand-write
  them. A Lite robot 404s; gate on `DaemonStatus.wireless_version`.
- `/update/ws/logs` sends each line as a text frame AND then a `JobInfo` JSON frame repeating those same lines —
  decode JSON first and ignore its `logs`, or every line doubles. The job ends with `systemctl restart`, which kills
  the daemon before a terminal `done`: the socket closing is completion, confirmed by reconnecting and comparing
  versions. `available_version: "unknown"` means the ROBOT could not reach PyPI, not that the check failed.
- The daemon's own source is installed at `.venv-sim/lib/python3.12/site-packages/reachy_mini/` — read
  `daemon/app/routers/*.py` and `daemon/app/services/bluetooth/` there rather than guessing a shape. It is a
  specification (project rule 1), never code to port.
- `/wifi/*` routes, from `routers/wifi_config.py`: `GET /wifi/prov_key`, **`POST`** `/wifi/scan_and_list` (a POST
  because it rescans first; uncapped, unlike the 180-byte BLE reply), `POST /wifi/connect_sealed`,
  `GET /wifi/status`, `GET /wifi/error`, `POST /wifi/reset_error`, `POST /wifi/forget?ssid=`, `POST /wifi/forget_all`.
  Plaintext `POST /wifi/connect?ssid=&password=` exists and must never be called — the PSK would go in a query string.
- `connect_sealed` answers `400 decrypt_failed` for a wrong PIN **and** for a `kid` older than the 600 s rotation, and
  409 while another `nmcli` operation runs. It returns immediately and joins on a background thread; on failure it
  removes the connection and re-raises its own hotspot, so the reason ends up in `GET /wifi/error`, not in the reply.
- `GET /wifi/status` is `{mode: hotspot|wlan|disconnected|busy, known_networks, connected_network}` — a joined station
  is `wlan`, not `connected`, and there is **no IP address in it**. The BLE status characteristic is the mirror image:
  live address, no network names. Neither contains the other.
- `POST /wifi/forget` answers 404 for a network the robot never saved and 400 for `Hotspot`. Everywhere else in
  `/wifi/*` and `/update/*` a 404 means the route was never mounted, i.e. a Lite robot.
- `GET /api/daemon/hardware-id` answers one key, `{"hardware_id": "<16 hex>"}` = `sha256(usb serial)[:16]` — the same
  string as mDNS TXT `unit_id` and BLE characteristic `…cdef7`. It is a join key: never reshape it.

## Bluetooth service

Read `services/bluetooth/bluetooth_service.py` in `.venv-sim` — the dispatch table is one `if/elif` chain and settles
most questions in a glance.

- It is **its own systemd unit** (`reachy-mini-bluetooth`, working directory `/bluetooth`), not part of the daemon.
  Every recovery script ends with `systemctl restart reachy-mini-daemon`, so the Bluetooth link survives all of them —
  including `SOFTWARE_RESET`, which erases `/venvs` while the service sits outside it. `PING` therefore proves the
  robot is there, never that a reset finished.
- The commands are exactly `PING`, `STATUS`, `JOURNAL_{START,READ,STOP}`, `PIN_*`, `UPDATE_{CHECK,START,INFO}`,
  `WIFI_{KEYEX,STATUS,SCAN,CONNECT_ENC,FORGET}`, `CMD_*`. Anything else falls through to `ECHO:`. **There is no
  `SET_NAME`** — renaming is `POST /api/daemon/robot-name` and needs the robot on a network.
- The PIN is the last five characters of the Pollen audio device's USB serial (`38fb:1001`, read from
  `/sys/bus/usb/devices/*/serial`), compared verbatim: not necessarily digits, never case-folded. Do not uppercase the
  input field. Upstream states that serial is printed on the robot — it is **not** a separate code, and no route
  exposes it, which is the point. With no audio board attached the daemon falls back to a fixed `46879`.
- `CMD_*` clears the robot's own auth flag in a `finally`, so the PIN is needed again after every script — whether it
  succeeded or not. Its handler also returns `None` on success, so the reply encoder crashes and the GATT write
  reports an error for a script that ran perfectly.
- `_read_journal` returns `buffer[:480]` and **deletes what it returned**. One BLE read carries ~182 bytes, so the
  remainder of every large chunk is lost for good, and a line is regularly cut in half — `BLEJournalReader` carries the
  tail. The LAN journal is the authoritative one; say so in any UI that shows this.
  - The journal is a byte stream, not a message, so `BLEResponseParser` returns `.payload` **verbatim**. Trimming it
    (as every other reply is trimmed) eats the trailing newline that says the last line is complete, and the reader
    then glues that line onto the next chunk — one corrupted line per read boundary, which looks like nothing at all
    when a chunk holds a single line.
  - `journalctl` exits on its own; the GLib watch removes itself on HUP and every later read answers
    `ERROR: Journal not running`. That is a `JOURNAL_START` away from fixed, not a terminal state.
- `…cdef6` is `", ".join(...)` over the robot's `commands/` directory with `.sh` stripped, `"None"` when empty, in
  `os.listdir` order. Read it; never hardcode the list, and sort it before showing it.

## MVP endpoint subset (what upstream actually calls)

`daemon/status|start|stop`, `daemon/hardware-id`, `daemon/robot-name`, `state/full`, `move/set_target`,
`move/play/wake_up`, `move/play/goto_sleep`, `move/play/recorded-move-dataset/{dataset}/{move}`,
`move/recorded-move-datasets/list/{dataset}`, `motors/set_mode/{mode}`, `apps/job-status/{id}`, `kinematics/info`.

## Timeouts (from upstream `src/config/daemon.ts` — battle-tested values)

- Healthcheck request timeout: 2 s (3.5 s over Wi-Fi); status poll every 3 s (5 s Wi-Fi).
- Connected-state hysteresis: require 2 consecutive successful probes to go "connected"; downgrade immediately on
  failure.
- Job polling: 500 ms; app install timeout 60 s, remove 90 s, start 120 s; stale-job 90 s.

## Facts

- Daemon process ≠ robot backend. `/api/daemon/status` answers 200 with `backend_status: null` while the backend is
  torn down (`daemon.stop()` sets `self.backend = None`); every route behind the `get_backend` dependency
  (`move/*`, `state/*` incl. `ws/full`, `motors/*`, `kinematics/*`, `volume/*`) answers **503 "Backend not running"**.
  `camera/*` uses `get_daemon` instead, and `/logs/ws/daemon` is mounted at the app root — both outside that gate.
- Wake/sleep are multi-step protocols, not single calls: `motors/set_mode/enabled` → 300 ms → `move/play/wake_up`;
  sleep reverses it (animation first, `set_mode/disabled` only after it finishes). The play routes never touch the
  motor mode — an asleep robot accepts them, plays the sound, and does not move.
- `daemon/start?wake_up=<bool>` returns a job id immediately and starts the backend in the background (409 while
  another job runs); poll `daemon/status` until `running`. With `wake_up=true` the daemon enables the motors itself.
- No MJPEG endpoint exists. Camera is WebRTC-only (signaling `ws://<host>:8443`, GStreamer webrtcsink, single H.264
  Constrained Baseline 3.1 stream, Opus audio, STUN `stun.l.google.com:19302`).
- Daemon 1.9.0 is the minimum and tested API baseline. Enforce
  `DaemonCompatibilityPolicy` during the first status handshake: reject older/different-major versions, warn for
  newer 1.x or unknown versions, and tolerate unknown JSON fields. See `docs/adr/0001-daemon-compatibility-and-lan-security.md`.
- The daemon has no authentication or encryption. v1 supports trusted private LAN/robot AP only; never imply that a
  client-side token adds security and never expose port 8000 publicly.
- 9 actuators: `body_rotation`, `stewart_1..6`, `left_antenna`, `right_antenna`. Safety limits are clamped server-side.
- `passive_joints` in the state stream is `null` unless the daemon was launched with `--kinematics-engine Placo`; the
  default `AnalyticalKinematics` never computes them and there is no API to switch engines. The 21 Stewart passive
  joints are therefore worked out client-side, for 3D visualization only. Upstream's `kinematics-wasm` crate describes
  the behavior to reproduce — read it as a specification, never as code to port.
- URDF + STL meshes are served by the daemon: `GET /api/kinematics/urdf` (a `{"urdf": "<xml>"}` object, ~250 KB) and
  `GET /api/kinematics/stl/{filename}` (raw bytes as `model/stl` — its docstring claiming to return a *path* is
  stale). The generated client cannot fetch the STL: it declares `application/json` for every response.
- `GET /api/kinematics/info` reports only `{"info": {"engine", "collision check"}}` — no joint names, no limits. Those
  live in the URDF alone.
- DoA angle (microphone direction of arrival) is in radians: 0 = left, π/2 = front/back, π = right.
- Speaker and microphone levels are `GET|POST /api/volume/{current,set}` and `/api/volume/microphone/{current,set}`,
  both `{"volume": 0…100}` in and `{volume, platform, device}` out. There is no separate "sensitivity" concept —
  microphone sensitivity *is* its input level. Wrapped as `AudioLevel`.
  - **`POST /api/volume/set` plays a test sound on every accepted call** (it is in the route's own description).
    Send it once a slider gesture ends, never on each change, or the robot beeps continuously.
  - Out-of-range values come back as 422, so both setters map `.unprocessableContent` explicitly.
  - On `sim-daemon` these routes drive the **host Mac's own** speaker and mic (`platform: Darwin`), not a robot.
    Note the level before testing and restore it after.

content.subject: M1.2 — RobotAppsClient protocol + RobotConnection+Apps
content.description: Sources/ReachyKit/Session/RobotAppsClient.swift (protocol with throwing defaults, DaemonUpdateClient template) and Sources/ReachyKit/Transport/RobotConnection+Apps.swift via the generated client. current-app-status returns literal null → must not go through the generated client's non-optional AppStatus decode. list-available hits HuggingFace → needs a longer budget than the 3.5 s handshake session.

content.subject: M1.3 — AppsManagerStreamClient (job log WebSocket)
content.description: ws /api/apps/ws/apps-manager/{job_id}. Same frame shapes as /update/ws/logs (bg_job_register.ws_poll_info serves both): raw text line frames then a JobInfo JSON frame, {"error":"Job ID not found"} + close for an unknown id, exactly one .closed. Share the streaming core with UpdateLogStreamClient rather than copying it.
content.activeForm: Building the job log stream client

content.subject: M1.4 — AppJobMonitor (WS + polling, injected clock)
content.description: Sources/ReachyKit/Session/AppJobMonitor.swift: WS stream plus job-status polling at 500 ms, timeouts install 60 s / remove 90 s / stale 90 s, outcome for "daemon restarted" (404 after a visible start). Injected clock — no fixed Task.sleep before assertions (project rule 7).

content.subject: M1.5 — RobotSession+Apps
content.description: canManageApps, withAppsClient {} (withWiFiClient template), catalog/installed caches following moves(in:refresh:).

content.subject: M1.6 — build, lint, format, commit
content.description: ./bin/mise run build && test (swift build --build-tests after test edits), lint, format-check, then a conventional commit for milestone M1.

content.subject: M2 — ReachyKit: hf-auth surface of the daemon
content.description: Model/HFAuth.swift (HFAuthStatus, RelayStatus with unavailable + unknown, RelayRefresh with the skipped trap, CentralRobotStatusProxy, CentralRobot), Session/HFAuthClient.swift, Transport/RobotConnection+HFAuth.swift, Session/RobotSession+HFAuth.swift (cached robotHFAccount, linkRobot, unlinkRobot). Token in the JSON body only — a test must prove it never reaches the URL. OAuth routes of the daemon are deliberately not wrapped.

content.subject: M4.1 — AppStoreModel with tests
content.description: Sources/ReachyUI/Apps/AppStoreModel.swift: Installed/Discover sections, search, coalescing loadID (MovesModel template), running-app banner state, startup-app toggle, update badges, robot-app-lock awareness. Tests in Tests/ReachyUITests.

content.subject: M4.2 — AppStoreScreen and the app card
content.description: AppStoreScreen.swift with the segmented picker, search (.searchable + .searchToolbarBehavior(.minimized) under #available(iOS 26)), emoji-on-gradient card, Official/private badges, running banner with Stop/Restart.

content.subject: M4.3 — AppInstallModel and the job overlay
content.description: SystemUpdateModel template: State enum (idle/installing/removing/updating/confirming/succeeded/failed/daemonRestarted), live log via LogConsoleModel, driven by AppJobMonitor, confirming poll of the installed list after done, seams for tests and previews.

content.subject: M4.4 — Tab bar: add Apps, drop Diagnostics
content.description: ReachyRootView: new Apps tab with a no-robot empty state; remove the Diagnostics tab and move SpikeView behind Settings → Developer (user decision, 2026-08-05). ReachyRootView's Diagnostics generic parameter and the ReachySpike app target change together.

content.subject: M4.5 — Previews and recorded snapshots
content.description: Project rule 8: a preview per state (store loading/empty/catalogue/installed+running/offline; overlay installing/failed/success), then mise run test:snapshots, then record, then an explicit git add of the LFS PNGs.

content.subject: M6 — Hugging Face account card and sign-in flow
content.description: Sources/ReachyUI/Settings/HFAccountSection.swift (WiFiSettingsCard template): signed-out with one-tap sign-in plus a paste-token fallback, signed-in with username and avatar, this robot's link state and relay status, Sign out. HFSignInModel + HFSignInFlow with an ASWebAuthenticationSession behind a @MainActor protocol seam so the model is testable and previews open nothing.
content.activeForm: Building the Hugging Face account UI

content.subject: M7 — Central relay client (SSE + POST)
content.description: Sources/ReachyKit/Central/CentralRelayClient.swift: GET /events read with URLSession.bytes, only data: lines decoded, POST /send whose reply body may itself be a signaling message, Bearer from an injected token provider, 60 s read timeout and 5→60 s backoff mirroring the robot's own relay, GET /api/robot-status for the robot list.

content.subject: M8.1 — RemoteControlChannel зелёный
content.description: Довести Tests/ReachyKitTests/RemoteControlChannelTests.swift до зелёного прогона (7 тестов), затем закоммитить Sources/ReachyKit/Central/RemoteControlChannel.swift. Прогон строго последовательный, один процесс SwiftPM за раз.

content.subject: M8.2 — RemoteRobotConnection поверх data-канала
content.description: Тип, реализующий RobotAPIClient через RemoteControlChannel. Карта команд проверена по исходникам даемона: handshake = get_version + get_hardware_id, daemonStatus/probeBackendReady = daemon_status, wake_up, goto_sleep, set_motor_mode, get_volume/set_volume, get_microphone_volume/set_microphone_volume, play_sound. Остальное наследует throwing-дефолты протокола — stop_sound, listMoves, playMove, urdf, kinematicsInfo, setRobotName в канале отсутствуют. ПОПРАВКА к плану: канала "pose" не существует, телеметрия идёт broadcast-ами по тому же каналу "data" и поля seq в ней нет — вместо дедупликации нужно прореживание потока 50 Гц.

content.subject: M8.3 — RemoteDataChannel поверх RTCDataChannel
content.description: В ReachyMedia: реализация RemoteDataChannel на RTCDataChannel. CameraSession.swift:305 peerConnection(_:didOpen:) сейчас пустышка. Робот открывает ровно ОДИН канал с меткой "data" (media_server.py:1712) — второго канала нет, ловить надо его.

content.subject: M9 — экран «Your Reachies» и удалённое подключение
content.description: ReachyUI: список роботов из central, степпер LINK → SESSION → WAKE-UP, обработка отказов через RemoteSessionEnd. Плюс превью и записанные снапшоты по правилу 8.

content.subject: M5 — виджеты (App Group, App Intents, extension)
content.description: Общий App Group для состояния робота, App Intents для команд, target виджет-расширения в Apps/Project.swift. Независимо от M8/M9.

content.subject: M10 — документация
content.description: ADR-0003 про удалённый доступ, docs/research/central-relay.md, обновление .claude/rules/, README. Плюс уже накопленные заметки в AGENTS.md.

content.subject: M9b — RobotSession без адреса, удалённое подключение
content.description: RobotSession.connect(using:) с готовым клиентом вместо makeClient(address). Сейчас connect привязан к адресу: KnownRobots.lastAddress, стрим состояния /api/state/ws/full, viewportAddress. У удалённой сессии адреса нет, телеметрия идёт broadcast-ами по data-каналу. Плюс сборка цепочки CentralSignalingTransport → CameraSession → WebRTCDataChannel → RemoteRobotConnection.

content.content:
[tasks.sim-daemon]
description = "Run simulated Reachy Mini daemon (MuJoCo) reachable from LAN devices"
run = """
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
# macOS: MuJoCo GUI requires mjpython, and uv has known MuJoCo issues — plain pip venv.
VENV=.venv-sim
REQUIREMENTS=Scripts/sim-requirements.txt
STAMP="$VENV/.requirements.sha256"
EXPECTED="$(shasum -a 256 "$REQUIREMENTS" | awk '{print $1}')"
# Explicit path: system PATH can shadow mise's python with an ancient one.
PYTHON="$(./bin/mise where python)/bin/python3"
INSTALLED="$(test -f "$STAMP" && cat "$STAMP" || true)"
if [ ! -x "$VENV/bin/mjpython" ] || [ "$INSTALLED" != "$EXPECTED" ]; then
  rm -rf "$VENV"
  "$PYTHON" -m venv "$VENV"
  "$VENV/bin/python" -m pip install --quiet --requirement "$REQUIREMENTS"
  printf '%s' "$EXPECTED" > "$STAMP"
fi
"$VENV/bin/python" -c 'import importlib.metadata as m; assert m.version("reachy-mini") == "1.9.0"'
# `gstreamer_python`'s libgstpython.dylib segfaults while GStreamer scans plugins.
# Forked (the default) that only surfaces as "External plugin loader failed" and
# the daemon then hangs before binding :8000; with GST_REGISTRY_FORK=no the
# segfault kills the daemon outright. The pipeline below needs native elements
# only, so the plugin is pure liability.
find "$VENV" -name libgstpython.dylib -exec mv {} {}.disabled ';' 2>/dev/null || true
# Without the scanner GStreamer's plugin loader silently fails, webrtcsink can't
# find the Opus encoder ("No caps found for stream audio_0") and no WebRTC
# producer is ever registered on :8443.
export GST_PLUGIN_SCANNER="$PWD/$VENV/lib/python3.12/site-packages/gstreamer_libs/libexec/gstreamer-1.0/gst-plugin-scanner"
exec "$VENV/bin/mjpython" -m reachy_mini.daemon.app.main --sim --fastapi-host 0.0.0.0 "$@"
"""

content.thinking:
Разбираюсь с предупреждениями в коде. `RemoteControlChannel` — это actor, и внутри него методы вроде `self.expire(token)`, `self.resume(...)`, `deliver(text)`, `failAll(...)` являются non-async, но вызываются на акторе. Интересует, наследует ли `Task`, созданный внутри actor-метода, контекст исполнения актора в Swift 6.

Оказывается, да — `Task {}` внутри актора наследует actor isolation, поэтому вызовы к `self` не требуют `await`. Отсюда и предупреждение про отсутствие async операций в await выражении. Но macOS-сборка через SwiftPM не выдала эти предупреждения, потому что используется другой компилятор (из .swift-version) чем Xcode — разные диагностики.

Это предупреждения, а не ошибки, но они указывают на важное: `Task {}` наследует изоляцию актора, значит `deadline` выполняется под защитой актора, что хорошо для корректности. `Task.sleep` внутри приостанавливает и освобождает актор. Но есть более тонкий момент с `startReading` и тем, как он создаёт Task...

Второе предупреждение про `try?` — это может быть реальная проблема с проглоченной ошибкой. Сборка на девайс прошла успешно, но появилось 5 предупреждений, которых нет в macOS-сборке. Стоит их чинить, потому что раньше целью было нулевое количество предупреждений, и они указывают на реальные проблемы — лишний await означает недопонимание изоляции, а unused try? означает проглоченную ошибку.

Но сначала нужно установить и запустить на устройстве, как просил пользователь, а потом разбираться с предупреждениями. Устанавливаю приложение и одновременно посмотрю на проблему в CentralRelayClient:216.

content.thinking:
Так вот в чём дело — предупреждения присутствуют в обоих тулчейнах, но инкрементальная сборка скрыла их, так как `mise run test` не перекомпилировал эти файлы. Моя гипотеза о расхождении тулчейнов оказалась неправильной, причина была проще, и я это подтвердил. Для sim-daemon логи совпадают с тем, что описано в комментарии mise.toml.

Теперь вижу ещё одну проблему — GStreamer не может найти плагин-сканер, хотя переменная окружения установлена, значит путь неверный или файл отсутствует. Это две отдельные находки: предупреждения в коде, которые я написал в этой ветке (регрессия чистоты сборки), и проблема с GStreamer.

Разбираюсь с предупреждениями в RemoteControlChannel — это actor, где Task наследует изоляцию актора, поэтому некоторые `await` вызовы избыточны, когда я уже нахожусь в контексте актора.

Исправление простое: убрать четыре лишних `await` и добавить `_ =` в CentralRelayClient:216. Это не просто косметика — это уточняет семантику, делая явным, что эти Task'и выполняются на акторе. Тесты подтверждают, что это безопасно.

Второй момент интереснее: `try? await send(...)` молча глотает ошибку анонса, и это может привести к невидимому сбою — пользователь увидит «подключено», но центральный сервер не узнает о пире, и сессия не состоится. Это дизайнерский выбор, где стоит спросить мнение пользователя.

Но сначала исправлю четыре механических предупреждения в RemoteControlChannel — проект держит планку warnings: 0, и это свежий код. Потом обсужу поведение при сбое анонса и разберусь с sim-daemon и GST_PLUGIN_SCANNER.

content.text:
Диагноз точный, и он не тот, что я предполагал: предупреждения есть **в обоих** тулчейнах — их прятала инкрементальная сборка, которая просто не перекомпилировала эти файлы. Сборка под устройство скомпилировала всё с нуля и показала правду.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
**`Task {}` внутри актора наследует его изоляцию.** Поэтому `await self.expire(token)` внутри `Task` в теле actor-метода — не кросс-акторный хоп, а обычный синхронный вызов: код уже на акторе. `await` там ничего не ждёт, и компилятор об этом говорит.

**Инкрементальная сборка прячет предупреждения.** Диагностика компилятора рождается только при фактической компиляции файла. `build_time: 20.32s` в зелёном прогоне означало, что эти файлы не пересобирались, а не что они чисты — «0 warnings» на инкрементальной сборке ничего не доказывает.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

Убираю четыре избыточных `await`.

# ReachyUI

Shared SwiftUI views for all platforms (macOS/iPadOS/iOS). Depends on ReachyKit and ReachyMedia (WebRTC camera).

- Adaptive layouts, not per-platform copies; `#if os(iOS)` only for platform-exclusive APIs (Settings deep link etc.).
- `horizontalSizeClass` is unavailable on macOS — guard size-class branching with `#if os(macOS)` (always regular there).
- All robot interaction goes through `RobotSession` / `RobotBrowser` from ReachyKit — no direct URLSession here.
- Screen logic belongs in a `@MainActor @Observable` model beside the view (`MovesModel`, `LogConsoleModel`), covered
  by `Tests/ReachyUITests`; the view stays thin. `@Observable` does honour `didSet`, so derived caches can live there.
- `Section` has no title-plus-footer overload: `Section("X") { … } footer: { … }` fails to compile with a misleading
  "generic parameter 'Content' could not be inferred". Either `Section("X") { … }` or the full
  `Section { … } header: { Text("X") } footer: { … }`.
- A container view taking a closure argument _and_ two trailing `@ViewBuilder`s trips SwiftLint's
  `multiple_closures_with_trailing_closure`. Pass the extra behaviour as a child view instead
  (`OnboardingBackButton`), not as a third closure.
- `background(_:)` defaults to `ignoresSafeAreaEdges: .all`, so a full-bleed backdrop also paints the inset the
  floating tab bar sits in — bottom on iPhone, top on iPad. That bar is glass and renders whatever it finds there, so
  it turns dark on that one tab, a frame behind the switch. State the edges (`ViewportView.backdropEdges`); bleed
  upwards only where a bar pinned to match is waiting for it (`darkTitleBar()`).
- Deployment floor is iOS 18 / macOS 15 (`Package.swift`, `Apps/Project.swift`), set by `RealityView`.
  `ScrollPosition`, `onScrollPhaseChange` and `onScrollGeometryChange` are available; the zero-height sentinel row in
  `LogConsoleScreen` predates the bump and is not a required pattern.

## Previews and snapshots

`Previews/` sits here but is **excluded from the SwiftPM target** (`Package.swift`) and compiled only by the Xcode
targets in `Apps/`. `#Preview` is an external macro implemented by `libPreviewsMacros.dylib`, which ships inside
Xcode's platform SDKs and not in the pinned swift.org toolchain — a `#Preview` anywhere under a SwiftPM target breaks
`mise run build`, `mise run test` and CI with "plugin for module 'PreviewsMacros' not found".

Adding a screen (project rule 8) means: a preview per state in `Previews/<Screen>Previews.swift`, whatever seam and
`#if DEBUG` factory those states need, `mise run test:snapshots:record`, and `git add` on the PNGs.

- Preview files use `@testable import ReachyUI`; that is why `ENABLE_TESTABILITY` is set for the whole Xcode project.
- **Prefire reads previews off the filesystem; Xcode compiles the file list Tuist baked in.** A new file under
  `Previews/` is therefore picked up by the generator but not compiled until `mise run project` runs again — which is
  why the snapshot tasks depend on it. A bare `xcodebuild` skips that and fails with "cannot find … in scope".
- Anything a preview body references must be visible target-wide, because Prefire copies the body into a separate
  generated file. Shared wrappers live in `PreviewScene`; a `private` helper compiles locally and breaks the test.
- **A preview with no `traits:` is captured at full device size.** Prefire defaults the trait list to `.device`
  (`RawPreviewModel.isScreen`), and that device trait is what carries `horizontalSizeClass` — so it is what makes the
  iPad snapshot exercise the regular-width layout. Components opt out with `traits: .sizeThatFitsLayout`.
- **A preview must be final on its first frame.** Prefire captures synchronously and its `.snapshot(delay:)` modifier
  lives in a module this target cannot import without breaking the macOS build. Never rely on a `.task` completing —
  hand the view a model that is already in its end state (`AudioSettingsModel.preview()`, `RobotSession.preview()`).
- Model preview factories live **in the model's own file** under `#if DEBUG`, not in `Previews/`: they write members
  that are `private` to that file, and `@testable` does not reach `private`.
- Screens take their model through an initialiser with a default (`init(session:model:)`), so production call sites
  are unchanged and previews inject a frozen one.
- A defaulted argument whose value is `@MainActor` (`= SpikeModel()`, `= .preview()`) compiles in the SwiftPM targets
  but not in the `Apps/` ones, where it is evaluated nonisolated. Use `nil` and resolve it in the body.
- A model that already takes a factory closure (`OnboardingModel(session:)`, `BLEConsoleModel(link:)`) needs no new
  seam — hand it a `BLELink.preview(…)`, which sits on an inert `PreviewBLETransport` and is assigned its state
  directly. Building the link is not enough on its own: `OnboardingModel.session` is only set by `beginScan()`, which
  is the CoreBluetooth call a preview must not make, so the factory assigns it.
- A screen whose `.task` guards on `model == nil` needs no `reachyPreviewMode` check — injecting the model is what
  makes it inert. Add the guard only where the effect runs unconditionally (`WiFiSettingsCard`, `LogConsoleScreen`).
- Not covered, deliberately: `SceneViewport` in `.ready` (a bare `RealityView`) and `CameraViewport` in `.streaming`
  (Metal-backed `RTCMTLVideoView`). Neither renders anything meaningful headless — snapshot their overlay phases.
- One `RobotSceneModel` per preview: `ReachyScene/AGENTS.md` requires exactly one live `RealityView` per model.
- **Navigation chrome does not stay inside a preview card.** SwiftUI hoists `.toolbar` and
  `.searchable` out of the storybook's scaled cards into the app's own bars, even though each
  preview brings its own `NavigationStack` — this is the limitation Prefire records as
  "NavigationView in Preview not supported for Playbook". The storybook hides its root bars to
  absorb it; `LogConsoleScreen`'s search field still floats over the catalogue, which is cosmetic
  and not worth contorting the screen for. Snapshots are unaffected — they capture the title _and_
  the toolbar items, so `RobotScreen`'s Settings gear and `MovesScreen`'s Refresh are covered.
  Only the storybook hoists.

content.thinking:
Так что проблема в том, что когда пользователь нажимает Sign in в Your Reachies без подключённого робота, это закрывает шторку и устанавливает флаг `showsSettings`, но никто его не обрабатывает, потому что `liveTab` не отображается в этом состоянии — это объясняет симптом.

Даже если бы вкладка была видна, TabView может не держать неактивные вкладки смонтированными, поэтому sheet всё равно не появился бы. Это структурная ошибка: sheet настроек должен быть на корневом уровне рядом с другим sheet'ом, а не внутри одной вкладки.

Но тут есть сложность с несколькими sheet'ами на одном view — они могут конфликтовать, и нельзя открыть второй, пока первый закрывается, потому что система ещё анимирует закрытие.

Правильное решение: перенести sheet настроек на уровень TabView и использовать `onDismiss` первого sheet'а, чтобы открыть второй только после полного закрытия. Или проще — показать вход в настройки прямо в шторке Your Reachies вместо того, чтобы выкидывать пользователя в отдельный экран.

Это два разных подхода с разными компромиссами: минимальный фикс текущего потока или улучшение UX с дополнительной работой. Стоит спросить пользователя, какой вариант ему нужен. Проверю логи устройства, хотя код уже достаточно ясен. Быстрее всего запустить в симуляторе и повторить сценарий, но это займёт время — юнит-тесты UI-навигацию не покрывают. Структурно доказательство прямое: `showsSettings` срабатывает только внутри `liveTab`, который не существует без подключённого робота, и симптом совпадает идеально. Проверю ещё, может ли `liveTab` вообще существовать без робота...

Вижу, что `viewportAddress` зависит от `session.isBackendRunning` — без подключения это nil, значит `liveTab` точно не создаётся. Теперь нужно решить: спросить пользователя про вариант решения или сразу дать минимальный фикс? Он прямо сейчас тестирует на устройстве и ждёт, поэтому лучше быстро починить и дать пересобрать, а вопрос про UX задать потом — минимальный фикс полезен в любом случае.

Хотя стоп — выбор варианта реально меняет поведение. Если выбрать вариант Б, то `signIn` вообще не будет открывать настройки, и минимальный фикс не понадобится, но sheet настроек всё равно сломан на корневом уровне. Если Б, то `showsSettings` из Your Reachies не вызывается и баг не проявляется, но кнопка настроек в liveTab всё ещё работает. Спрошу коротко с рекомендацией, но пользователь уже просил перейти к следующей задаче.

Задам точный вопрос с рекомендацией варианта Б, потому что это устраняет и баг, и странный UX. Для этого нужно перенести HF sign-in UI в Your Reachies — есть готовый компонент `HFAccountCard` в Settings, который можно переиспользовать. Сначала проверю структуру, чтобы вопрос был обоснованным.

content.thinking:
So `SettingsScreen` includes a ready-made `HFAccountSection` component that pulls the `hfAccount` from the environment. There's an interesting consideration here — since `SettingsScreen` is the robot's settings screen, it might be mostly empty if the robot isn't connected. The `HFAccount` itself comes through the environment via `.environment(hfAccount)` passed down on the TabView.

Now I'm weighing two approaches. Option A is a minimal fix: move the `.sheet(isPresented: $showsSettings)` up to the root level on TabView alongside the "Your Reachies" sheet, then handle the sequential sheets issue with `onDismiss`. Option B is more elegant — replace the "Sign in" button with a direct navigation to `HFAccountSection` (or a compact login screen) inside the "Your Reachies" sheet itself using the existing NavigationStack. Option B feels better for UX since the user stays in context and the list updates automatically after login, plus it avoids the fragility of juggling two sheets in SwiftUI. It's straightforward to implement too — just swap the sign-in closure for a NavigationLink pointing to a login screen within the same stack. I need to check `HFAccountSection`'s signature to see if it requires `session`. The real question is whether I should even ask the user, since there's a strong case that option B is obviously the right choice — keeping the user in context is the natural pattern here.

content.subject: M1.1 — RobotApps domain model + shared DaemonJob
content.description: Sources/ReachyKit/Model/RobotApps.swift: RobotApp wrapper over Components.Schemas.AppInfo with extra parsing (spaceID, title, emoji, gradient, author, likes, isPrivate, isOfficial), RobotAppStatus with unknown(String) state, StartupApp, AppUpdatesSummary, RobotAppLockStatus, identity matching. Extract DaemonJob from DaemonUpdate.swift with typealias DaemonUpdateJob = DaemonJob. Tests first.

content.subject: M1.2 — RobotAppsClient protocol + RobotConnection+Apps
content.description: Sources/ReachyKit/Session/RobotAppsClient.swift (protocol with throwing defaults, DaemonUpdateClient template) and Sources/ReachyKit/Transport/RobotConnection+Apps.swift via the generated client. current-app-status returns literal null → must not go through the generated client's non-optional AppStatus decode. list-available hits HuggingFace → needs a longer budget than the 3.5 s handshake session.

content.subject: M1.3 — AppsManagerStreamClient (job log WebSocket)
content.description: ws /api/apps/ws/apps-manager/{job_id}. Same frame shapes as /update/ws/logs (bg_job_register.ws_poll_info serves both): raw text line frames then a JobInfo JSON frame, {"error":"Job ID not found"} + close for an unknown id, exactly one .closed. Share the streaming core with UpdateLogStreamClient rather than copying it.
content.activeForm: Building the job log stream client

content.subject: M1.4 — AppJobMonitor (WS + polling, injected clock)
content.description: Sources/ReachyKit/Session/AppJobMonitor.swift: WS stream plus job-status polling at 500 ms, timeouts install 60 s / remove 90 s / stale 90 s, outcome for "daemon restarted" (404 after a visible start). Injected clock — no fixed Task.sleep before assertions (project rule 7).

content.subject: M1.5 — RobotSession+Apps
content.description: canManageApps, withAppsClient {} (withWiFiClient template), catalog/installed caches following moves(in:refresh:).

content.subject: M1.6 — build, lint, format, commit
content.description: ./bin/mise run build && test (swift build --build-tests after test edits), lint, format-check, then a conventional commit for milestone M1.

content.subject: M2 — ReachyKit: hf-auth surface of the daemon
content.description: Model/HFAuth.swift (HFAuthStatus, RelayStatus with unavailable + unknown, RelayRefresh with the skipped trap, CentralRobotStatusProxy, CentralRobot), Session/HFAuthClient.swift, Transport/RobotConnection+HFAuth.swift, Session/RobotSession+HFAuth.swift (cached robotHFAccount, linkRobot, unlinkRobot). Token in the JSON body only — a test must prove it never reaches the URL. OAuth routes of the daemon are deliberately not wrapped.

content.subject: M4.1 — AppStoreModel with tests
content.description: Sources/ReachyUI/Apps/AppStoreModel.swift: Installed/Discover sections, search, coalescing loadID (MovesModel template), running-app banner state, startup-app toggle, update badges, robot-app-lock awareness. Tests in Tests/ReachyUITests.

content.subject: M4.2 — AppStoreScreen and the app card
content.description: AppStoreScreen.swift with the segmented picker, search (.searchable + .searchToolbarBehavior(.minimized) under #available(iOS 26)), emoji-on-gradient card, Official/private badges, running banner with Stop/Restart.

content.subject: M4.3 — AppInstallModel and the job overlay
content.description: SystemUpdateModel template: State enum (idle/installing/removing/updating/confirming/succeeded/failed/daemonRestarted), live log via LogConsoleModel, driven by AppJobMonitor, confirming poll of the installed list after done, seams for tests and previews.

content.subject: M4.4 — Tab bar: add Apps, drop Diagnostics
content.description: ReachyRootView: new Apps tab with a no-robot empty state; remove the Diagnostics tab and move SpikeView behind Settings → Developer (user decision, 2026-08-05). ReachyRootView's Diagnostics generic parameter and the ReachySpike app target change together.

content.subject: M4.5 — Previews and recorded snapshots
content.description: Project rule 8: a preview per state (store loading/empty/catalogue/installed+running/offline; overlay installing/failed/success), then mise run test:snapshots, then record, then an explicit git add of the LFS PNGs.

content.subject: M6 — Hugging Face account card and sign-in flow
content.description: Sources/ReachyUI/Settings/HFAccountSection.swift (WiFiSettingsCard template): signed-out with one-tap sign-in plus a paste-token fallback, signed-in with username and avatar, this robot's link state and relay status, Sign out. HFSignInModel + HFSignInFlow with an ASWebAuthenticationSession behind a @MainActor protocol seam so the model is testable and previews open nothing.
content.activeForm: Building the Hugging Face account UI

content.subject: M7 — Central relay client (SSE + POST)
content.description: Sources/ReachyKit/Central/CentralRelayClient.swift: GET /events read with URLSession.bytes, only data: lines decoded, POST /send whose reply body may itself be a signaling message, Bearer from an injected token provider, 60 s read timeout and 5→60 s backoff mirroring the robot's own relay, GET /api/robot-status for the robot list.

content.subject: M8.1 — RemoteControlChannel зелёный
content.description: Довести Tests/ReachyKitTests/RemoteControlChannelTests.swift до зелёного прогона (7 тестов), затем закоммитить Sources/ReachyKit/Central/RemoteControlChannel.swift. Прогон строго последовательный, один процесс SwiftPM за раз.

content.subject: M8.2 — RemoteRobotConnection поверх data-канала
content.description: Тип, реализующий RobotAPIClient через RemoteControlChannel. Карта команд проверена по исходникам даемона: handshake = get_version + get_hardware_id, daemonStatus/probeBackendReady = daemon_status, wake_up, goto_sleep, set_motor_mode, get_volume/set_volume, get_microphone_volume/set_microphone_volume, play_sound. Остальное наследует throwing-дефолты протокола — stop_sound, listMoves, playMove, urdf, kinematicsInfo, setRobotName в канале отсутствуют. ПОПРАВКА к плану: канала "pose" не существует, телеметрия идёт broadcast-ами по тому же каналу "data" и поля seq в ней нет — вместо дедупликации нужно прореживание потока 50 Гц.

content.subject: M8.3 — RemoteDataChannel поверх RTCDataChannel
content.description: В ReachyMedia: реализация RemoteDataChannel на RTCDataChannel. CameraSession.swift:305 peerConnection(_:didOpen:) сейчас пустышка. Робот открывает ровно ОДИН канал с меткой "data" (media_server.py:1712) — второго канала нет, ловить надо его.

content.subject: M9 — экран «Your Reachies» и удалённое подключение
content.description: ReachyUI: список роботов из central, степпер LINK → SESSION → WAKE-UP, обработка отказов через RemoteSessionEnd. Плюс превью и записанные снапшоты по правилу 8.

content.subject: M5 — виджеты (App Group, App Intents, extension)
content.description: Общий App Group для состояния робота, App Intents для команд, target виджет-расширения в Apps/Project.swift. Независимо от M8/M9.

content.subject: M10 — документация
content.description: ADR-0003 про удалённый доступ, docs/research/central-relay.md, обновление .claude/rules/, README. Плюс уже накопленные заметки в AGENTS.md.

content.subject: M9b — RobotSession без адреса, удалённое подключение
content.description: RobotSession.connect(using:) с готовым клиентом вместо makeClient(address). Сейчас connect привязан к адресу: KnownRobots.lastAddress, стрим состояния /api/state/ws/full, viewportAddress. У удалённой сессии адреса нет, телеметрия идёт broadcast-ами по data-каналу. Теперь я вижу полную картину и готов к реализации. Нужно переделать `YourReachiesScreen`, заменив свойство `signIn` с простого замыкания на `@ViewBuilder`, который возвращает `SignIn`, и использовать `NavigationLink` вместо `Button`. Есть два места, где вызывается `signIn` — в состояниях `.signedOut` и `.needsSignIn`, оба должны вести на один и тот же экран.

Дальше нужно обновить `ReachyRootView`, чтобы передать правильный destination, создать новый экран `HFSignInScreen` с формой и `HFAccountSection`, и добавить превью. Важный момент: `HFAccountSection` показывает секцию только если `session.canLinkHuggingFace`, что в удалённом сценарии не будет выполнено. Но есть нюанс с визуальным отличием — `NavigationLink` в `ContentUnavailableView` будет выглядеть как ссылка с шевроном, а не как обычная кнопка с `.borderedProminent` стилем, поэтому эталоны для состояний signed out и session expired изменятся. Defining the generic view structure... Checking the naming — HFSignInScreen is unique, so I'll place it in Settings alongside HFSignInModel for consistency. Now I'm building the screen itself as a simple wrapper that reuses HFAccountSection, which handles both the robot connection display and the sign-in flow within a Form. Так как HFSignInModel создаётся в замыкании signIn, она будет пересоздаваться при каждом рендере, но HFAccountSection хранит её в @State и инициализирует из переданной, поэтому пересоздание не критично — State сохранит первый экземпляр. Теперь проверю результат на симуляторе и начну писать код в таком порядке: новый HFSignInScreen, затем обновлю YourReachiesScreen как generic, и наконец ReachyRootView с передачей destination.

content.subject: M1.1 — RobotApps domain model + shared DaemonJob
content.description: Sources/ReachyKit/Model/RobotApps.swift: RobotApp wrapper over Components.Schemas.AppInfo with extra parsing (spaceID, title, emoji, gradient, author, likes, isPrivate, isOfficial), RobotAppStatus with unknown(String) state, StartupApp, AppUpdatesSummary, RobotAppLockStatus, identity matching. Extract DaemonJob from DaemonUpdate.swift with typealias DaemonUpdateJob = DaemonJob. Tests first.

content.subject: M1.2 — RobotAppsClient protocol + RobotConnection+Apps
content.description: Sources/ReachyKit/Session/RobotAppsClient.swift (protocol with throwing defaults, DaemonUpdateClient template) and Sources/ReachyKit/Transport/RobotConnection+Apps.swift via the generated client. current-app-status returns literal null → must not go through the generated client's non-optional AppStatus decode. list-available hits HuggingFace → needs a longer budget than the 3.5 s handshake session.

content.subject: M1.3 — AppsManagerStreamClient (job log WebSocket)
content.description: ws /api/apps/ws/apps-manager/{job_id}. Same frame shapes as /update/ws/logs (bg_job_register.ws_poll_info serves both): raw text line frames then a JobInfo JSON frame, {"error":"Job ID not found"} + close for an unknown id, exactly one .closed. Share the streaming core with UpdateLogStreamClient rather than copying it.
content.activeForm: Building the job log stream client

content.subject: M1.4 — AppJobMonitor (WS + polling, injected clock)
content.description: Sources/ReachyKit/Session/AppJobMonitor.swift: WS stream plus job-status polling at 500 ms, timeouts install 60 s / remove 90 s / stale 90 s, outcome for "daemon restarted" (404 after a visible start). Injected clock — no fixed Task.sleep before assertions (project rule 7).

content.subject: M1.5 — RobotSession+Apps
content.description: canManageApps, withAppsClient {} (withWiFiClient template), catalog/installed caches following moves(in:refresh:).

content.subject: M1.6 — build, lint, format, commit
content.description: ./bin/mise run build && test (swift build --build-tests after test edits), lint, format-check, then a conventional commit for milestone M1.

content.subject: M2 — ReachyKit: hf-auth surface of the daemon
content.description: Model/HFAuth.swift (HFAuthStatus, RelayStatus with unavailable + unknown, RelayRefresh with the skipped trap, CentralRobotStatusProxy, CentralRobot), Session/HFAuthClient.swift, Transport/RobotConnection+HFAuth.swift, Session/RobotSession+HFAuth.swift (cached robotHFAccount, linkRobot, unlinkRobot). Token in the JSON body only — a test must prove it never reaches the URL. OAuth routes of the daemon are deliberately not wrapped.

content.subject: M4.1 — AppStoreModel with tests
content.description: Sources/ReachyUI/Apps/AppStoreModel.swift: Installed/Discover sections, search, coalescing loadID (MovesModel template), running-app banner state, startup-app toggle, update badges, robot-app-lock awareness. Tests in Tests/ReachyUITests.

content.subject: M4.2 — AppStoreScreen and the app card
content.description: AppStoreScreen.swift with the segmented picker, search (.searchable + .searchToolbarBehavior(.minimized) under #available(iOS 26)), emoji-on-gradient card, Official/private badges, running banner with Stop/Restart.

content.subject: M4.3 — AppInstallModel and the job overlay
content.description: SystemUpdateModel template: State enum (idle/installing/removing/updating/confirming/succeeded/failed/daemonRestarted), live log via LogConsoleModel, driven by AppJobMonitor, confirming poll of the installed list after done, seams for tests and previews.

content.subject: M4.4 — Tab bar: add Apps, drop Diagnostics
content.description: ReachyRootView: new Apps tab with a no-robot empty state; remove the Diagnostics tab and move SpikeView behind Settings → Developer (user decision, 2026-08-05). ReachyRootView's Diagnostics generic parameter and the ReachySpike app target change together.

content.subject: M4.5 — Previews and recorded snapshots
content.description: Project rule 8: a preview per state (store loading/empty/catalogue/installed+running/offline; overlay installing/failed/success), then mise run test:snapshots, then record, then an explicit git add of the LFS PNGs.

content.subject: M6 — Hugging Face account card and sign-in flow
content.description: Sources/ReachyUI/Settings/HFAccountSection.swift (WiFiSettingsCard template): signed-out with one-tap sign-in plus a paste-token fallback, signed-in with username and avatar, this robot's link state and relay status, Sign out. HFSignInModel + HFSignInFlow with an ASWebAuthenticationSession behind a @MainActor protocol seam so the model is testable and previews open nothing.
content.activeForm: Building the Hugging Face account UI

content.subject: M7 — Central relay client (SSE + POST)
content.description: Sources/ReachyKit/Central/CentralRelayClient.swift: GET /events read with URLSession.bytes, only data: lines decoded, POST /send whose reply body may itself be a signaling message, Bearer from an injected token provider, 60 s read timeout and 5→60 s backoff mirroring the robot's own relay, GET /api/robot-status for the robot list.

content.subject: M8.1 — RemoteControlChannel зелёный
content.description: Довести Tests/ReachyKitTests/RemoteControlChannelTests.swift до зелёного прогона (7 тестов), затем закоммитить Sources/ReachyKit/Central/RemoteControlChannel.swift. Прогон строго последовательный, один процесс SwiftPM за раз.

content.subject: M8.2 — RemoteRobotConnection поверх data-канала
content.description: Тип, реализующий RobotAPIClient через RemoteControlChannel. Карта команд проверена по исходникам даемона: handshake = get_version + get_hardware_id, daemonStatus/probeBackendReady = daemon_status, wake_up, goto_sleep, set_motor_mode, get_volume/set_volume, get_microphone_volume/set_microphone_volume, play_sound. Остальное наследует throwing-дефолты протокола — stop_sound, listMoves, playMove, urdf, kinematicsInfo, setRobotName в канале отсутствуют. ПОПРАВКА к плану: канала "pose" не существует, телеметрия идёт broadcast-ами по тому же каналу "data" и поля seq в ней нет — вместо дедупликации нужно прореживание потока 50 Гц.

content.subject: M8.3 — RemoteDataChannel поверх RTCDataChannel
content.description: В ReachyMedia: реализация RemoteDataChannel на RTCDataChannel. CameraSession.swift:305 peerConnection(_:didOpen:) сейчас пустышка. Робот открывает ровно ОДИН канал с меткой "data" (media_server.py:1712) — второго канала нет, ловить надо его.

content.subject: M9 — экран «Your Reachies» и удалённое подключение
content.description: ReachyUI: список роботов из central, степпер LINK → SESSION → WAKE-UP, обработка отказов через RemoteSessionEnd. Плюс превью и записанные снапшоты по правилу 8.

content.subject: M5 — виджеты (App Group, App Intents, extension)
content.description: Общий App Group для состояния робота, App Intents для команд, target виджет-расширения в Apps/Project.swift. Независимо от M8/M9.

content.subject: M10 — документация
content.description: ADR-0003 про удалённый доступ, docs/research/central-relay.md, обновление .claude/rules/, README. Плюс уже накопленные заметки в AGENTS.md.

content.subject: M9b — RobotSession без адреса, удалённое подключение
content.description: RobotSession.connect(using:) с готовым клиентом вместо makeClient(address). Сейчас connect привязан к адресу: KnownRobots.lastAddress, стрим состояния /api/state/ws/full, viewportAddress. У удалённой сессии адреса нет, телеметрия идёт broadcast-ами по data-каналу. Плюс сборка цепочки CentralSignalingTransport → CameraSession → WebRTCDataChannel → RemoteRobotConnection.

- `06:39:06` — пайплайн робота падает: `No caps found for stream audio_0`, «нет кодека для типа потока»
- `06:41:03` — только через две минуты подключается наш клиент, корректно регистрируется (`registered as [Listener]`) и запрашивает список

content.subject: M1.1 — RobotApps domain model + shared DaemonJob
content.description: Sources/ReachyKit/Model/RobotApps.swift: RobotApp wrapper over Components.Schemas.AppInfo with extra parsing (spaceID, title, emoji, gradient, author, likes, isPrivate, isOfficial), RobotAppStatus with unknown(String) state, StartupApp, AppUpdatesSummary, RobotAppLockStatus, identity matching. Extract DaemonJob from DaemonUpdate.swift with typealias DaemonUpdateJob = DaemonJob. Tests first.

content.subject: M1.2 — RobotAppsClient protocol + RobotConnection+Apps
content.description: Sources/ReachyKit/Session/RobotAppsClient.swift (protocol with throwing defaults, DaemonUpdateClient template) and Sources/ReachyKit/Transport/RobotConnection+Apps.swift via the generated client. current-app-status returns literal null → must not go through the generated client's non-optional AppStatus decode. list-available hits HuggingFace → needs a longer budget than the 3.5 s handshake session.

content.subject: M1.3 — AppsManagerStreamClient (job log WebSocket)
content.description: ws /api/apps/ws/apps-manager/{job_id}. Same frame shapes as /update/ws/logs (bg_job_register.ws_poll_info serves both): raw text line frames then a JobInfo JSON frame, {"error":"Job ID not found"} + close for an unknown id, exactly one .closed. Share the streaming core with UpdateLogStreamClient rather than copying it.
content.activeForm: Building the job log stream client

content.subject: M1.4 — AppJobMonitor (WS + polling, injected clock)
content.description: Sources/ReachyKit/Session/AppJobMonitor.swift: WS stream plus job-status polling at 500 ms, timeouts install 60 s / remove 90 s / stale 90 s, outcome for "daemon restarted" (404 after a visible start). Injected clock — no fixed Task.sleep before assertions (project rule 7).

content.subject: M1.5 — RobotSession+Apps
content.description: canManageApps, withAppsClient {} (withWiFiClient template), catalog/installed caches following moves(in:refresh:).

content.subject: M1.6 — build, lint, format, commit
content.description: ./bin/mise run build && test (swift build --build-tests after test edits), lint, format-check, then a conventional commit for milestone M1.

content.subject: M2 — ReachyKit: hf-auth surface of the daemon
content.description: Model/HFAuth.swift (HFAuthStatus, RelayStatus with unavailable + unknown, RelayRefresh with the skipped trap, CentralRobotStatusProxy, CentralRobot), Session/HFAuthClient.swift, Transport/RobotConnection+HFAuth.swift, Session/RobotSession+HFAuth.swift (cached robotHFAccount, linkRobot, unlinkRobot). Token in the JSON body only — a test must prove it never reaches the URL. OAuth routes of the daemon are deliberately not wrapped.

content.subject: M4.1 — AppStoreModel with tests
content.description: Sources/ReachyUI/Apps/AppStoreModel.swift: Installed/Discover sections, search, coalescing loadID (MovesModel template), running-app banner state, startup-app toggle, update badges, robot-app-lock awareness. Tests in Tests/ReachyUITests.

content.subject: M4.2 — AppStoreScreen and the app card
content.description: AppStoreScreen.swift with the segmented picker, search (.searchable + .searchToolbarBehavior(.minimized) under #available(iOS 26)), emoji-on-gradient card, Official/private badges, running banner with Stop/Restart.

content.subject: M4.3 — AppInstallModel and the job overlay
content.description: SystemUpdateModel template: State enum (idle/installing/removing/updating/confirming/succeeded/failed/daemonRestarted), live log via LogConsoleModel, driven by AppJobMonitor, confirming poll of the installed list after done, seams for tests and previews.

content.subject: M4.4 — Tab bar: add Apps, drop Diagnostics
content.description: ReachyRootView: new Apps tab with a no-robot empty state; remove the Diagnostics tab and move SpikeView behind Settings → Developer (user decision, 2026-08-05). ReachyRootView's Diagnostics generic parameter and the ReachySpike app target change together.

content.subject: M4.5 — Previews and recorded snapshots
content.description: Project rule 8: a preview per state (store loading/empty/catalogue/installed+running/offline; overlay installing/failed/success), then mise run test:snapshots, then record, then an explicit git add of the LFS PNGs.

content.subject: M6 — Hugging Face account card and sign-in flow
content.description: Sources/ReachyUI/Settings/HFAccountSection.swift (WiFiSettingsCard template): signed-out with one-tap sign-in plus a paste-token fallback, signed-in with username and avatar, this robot's link state and relay status, Sign out. HFSignInModel + HFSignInFlow with an ASWebAuthenticationSession behind a @MainActor protocol seam so the model is testable and previews open nothing.
content.activeForm: Building the Hugging Face account UI

content.subject: M7 — Central relay client (SSE + POST)
content.description: Sources/ReachyKit/Central/CentralRelayClient.swift: GET /events read with URLSession.bytes, only data: lines decoded, POST /send whose reply body may itself be a signaling message, Bearer from an injected token provider, 60 s read timeout and 5→60 s backoff mirroring the robot's own relay, GET /api/robot-status for the robot list.

content.subject: M8.1 — RemoteControlChannel зелёный
content.description: Довести Tests/ReachyKitTests/RemoteControlChannelTests.swift до зелёного прогона (7 тестов), затем закоммитить Sources/ReachyKit/Central/RemoteControlChannel.swift. Прогон строго последовательный, один процесс SwiftPM за раз.

content.subject: M8.2 — RemoteRobotConnection поверх data-канала
content.description: Тип, реализующий RobotAPIClient через RemoteControlChannel. Карта команд проверена по исходникам даемона: handshake = get_version + get_hardware_id, daemonStatus/probeBackendReady = daemon_status, wake_up, goto_sleep, set_motor_mode, get_volume/set_volume, get_microphone_volume/set_microphone_volume, play_sound. Остальное наследует throwing-дефолты протокола — stop_sound, listMoves, playMove, urdf, kinematicsInfo, setRobotName в канале отсутствуют. ПОПРАВКА к плану: канала "pose" не существует, телеметрия идёт broadcast-ами по тому же каналу "data" и поля seq в ней нет — вместо дедупликации нужно прореживание потока 50 Гц.

content.subject: M8.3 — RemoteDataChannel поверх RTCDataChannel
content.description: В ReachyMedia: реализация RemoteDataChannel на RTCDataChannel. CameraSession.swift:305 peerConnection(_:didOpen:) сейчас пустышка. Робот открывает ровно ОДИН канал с меткой "data" (media_server.py:1712) — второго канала нет, ловить надо его.

content.subject: M9 — экран «Your Reachies» и удалённое подключение
content.description: ReachyUI: список роботов из central, степпер LINK → SESSION → WAKE-UP, обработка отказов через RemoteSessionEnd. Плюс превью и записанные снапшоты по правилу 8.

content.subject: M5 — виджеты (App Group, App Intents, extension)
content.description: Общий App Group для состояния робота, App Intents для команд, target виджет-расширения в Apps/Project.swift. Независимо от M8/M9.

content.subject: M10 — документация
content.description: ADR-0003 про удалённый доступ, docs/research/central-relay.md, обновление .claude/rules/, README. Плюс уже накопленные заметки в AGENTS.md.

content.subject: M9b — RobotSession без адреса, удалённое подключение
content.description: RobotSession.connect(using:) с готовым клиентом вместо makeClient(address). Сейчас connect привязан к адресу: KnownRobots.lastAddress, стрим состояния /api/state/ws/full, viewportAddress. У удалённой сессии адреса нет, телеметрия идёт broadcast-ами по data-каналу. Плюс сборка цепочки CentralSignalingTransport → CameraSession → WebRTCDataChannel → RemoteRobotConnection.

Five axes, one process at a time: SwiftLint strict, format-check (hk), full swift test, ReachySpike app target, snapshot references. Plus two runtime checks the automated axes cannot give: SimulatorIntegrationTests against a live sim-daemon (guards the RobotSession connect-path refactor from M9b), and a real device build/install/launch on the iPhone 17 Pro.</description>
