content.text:
Здесь настоящий внешний блокер, и он требует вашего действия. Диагноз точный:

```
Provisioning profile "iOS Team Provisioning Profile: *" doesn't include the App Groups capability
No Accounts: Add a new account in Accounts settings
```

**Wildcard-профиль (`*`) не может содержать App Groups** — для этого нужен explicit App ID. Раньше сборки на устройство проходили именно потому, что хватало wildcard. Создать explicit App ID и саму группу `group.com.alexey1312.ReachyMini` может только владелец аккаунта, а `xcodebuild` из командной строки аккаунт не видит.

Что нужно от вас (один раз):

```bash
open Apps/ReachyMiniApps.xcworkspace
```

Дальше — таргет **ReachySpike** → **Signing & Capabilities** → **+ Capability** → **App Groups** → добавить `group.com.alexey1312.ReachyMini`. Xcode сам создаст App ID и группу в аккаунте. После этого сборка из CLI пойдёт.

Это не ломает остальное: macOS-таргет уже собрался с этим entitlement (`errors: 0`), тесты зелёные, симулятор подпись не проверяет. Так что **я не блокируюсь** — продолжаю M5.2, а устройство проверим, когда группа появится в аккаунте.

Состояние M5.1: код готов и покрыт — 6 новых тестов на миграцию (перенос роботов и последнего адреса, однократность, сохранность старого хранилища, чистая установка, фолбэк без entitlement), всего **549** зелёных. Идентификатор группы читается из Info.plist, а не зашит в библиотеку: `ReachyKit` не должен знать идентификаторы одного разработчицкого аккаунта, и расширение объявит тот же ключ у себя.

Перехожу к снимку состояния для виджета.

content.thinking:
M5.1 is committed. Now I'm working on M5.2, which defines a snapshot structure that captures the robot's state for the widget — including the robot name, whether it's awake, what app is running, and when the snapshot was taken.

I'm also building a store to persist these snapshots using UserDefaults, and adding logic to determine if a snapshot has become stale. The key insight is that when data gets old, the widget should display "no fresh data" rather than showing outdated information as current.

Now I'm deciding on a reasonable staleness threshold — considering that the app only writes snapshots when changes occur, and the robot could power down at any time. Something like 15 minutes or an hour seems reasonable, but I'm thinking through the user experience: if they haven't opened the app in a day, the data is meaningless, but if it was updated 10 minutes ago, it's probably still accurate since robots don't change state that frequently.

I'll use 30 minutes as the threshold but make it configurable. Actually, a better approach is to always show the timestamp ("2 hours ago") and only mark it stale after crossing that threshold, at which point I won't assert the state as current.

content.thinking:
Я вижу, что `startPolling` обновляет `lastStatus` каждый интервал — это идеальное место для снимка состояния. `isAwake` вычисляется из `lastStatus` как комбинация `isBackendRunning && motorMode == .enabled`. Проблема в том, что `currentApp()` — это асинхронный запрос без кэширования в сессии, поэтому вызывать его в polling каждые N секунд неэффективно.

Решаю прагматично: снимок пишется в polling без `runningApp` (nil), а при явных действиях с приложениями — с именем. Это честнее, чем хранить устаревшее имя или делать лишние запросы.

Для реализации создаю метод, который записывает снимок с известными данными сессии — имя робота, статус бодрствования и время, плюс опционально имя приложения, если оно доступно. Но нужно учесть, что `Date()` недетерминирована для тестов.

Добавляю параметр даты в сигнатуру метода, чтобы можно было инжектировать её при тестировании. Вызывать снимок нужно в трёх местах: при завершении подключения, в polling после обновления статуса и при разрыве соединения. Пока что для `runningApp` буду передавать `nil`, так как основная информация (имя робота, время, статус) уже даёт пользователю полезный виджет, а имя приложения — это приятный бонус, который можно добавить позже.

Решение: кэшировать последнее известное приложение в сессии, обновляемое из UI, и передавать его в снимок. Но AppStoreModel дёргает currentApp() только когда открыт магазин, поэтому в первой версии просто оставлю поле опциональным в модели — оно уже есть в тестах. Виджет покажет имя приложения, если оно доступно, а в polling буду передавать сохранённое значение из текущего снимка, чтобы не потерять информацию. Я понимаю проблему: после старта приложение появится в снимке, но при следующем опросе исчезнет. Лучше убрать `runningApp` из модели на этом этапе — это упростит логику и сделает её честнее. Тесты придётся переписать, но это стоит того, чтобы избежать путаницы с кэшированием и обновлением данных.

Окончательное решение: сессия всегда пишет `runningApp: nil`, поле остаётся в модели для будущего расширения, виджет показывает имя робота, состояние и время. Тест на round-trip модели остаётся валидным, так как проверяет сохранение полей.

Теперь реализую интеграцию RobotSession со снимками — сначала напишу тесты для проверки, что снимок записывается после подключения и очищается после отключения.

content.description: Тип, реализующий RobotAPIClient через RemoteControlChannel. content.subject: Verify the whole branch before starting M5
content.description:
Five axes, one process at a time: SwiftLint strict, format-check (hk), full swift test, ReachySpike app target, snapshot references. Plus two runtime checks the automated axes cannot give: SimulatorIntegrationTests against a live sim-daemon (guards the RobotSession connect-path refactor from M9b), and a real device build/install/launch on the iPhone 17 Pro.</description>
<parameter name="activeForm">Verifying the branch before M5

content.subject: ADR 0003 — remote access over the Hugging Face relay
content.description:
Record the decisions already shipped and verified: HF as this app's own account (public OAuth client + PKCE, token in Keychain, live sign-in confirmed on device), the central relay as SSE + POST, the WebRTC data channel as the remote control surface, reply correlation on a wire with no request ids, assembled DaemonStatus, and what the remote path deliberately cannot do (3D scene, /wifi, /update, rename).</description>
<parameter name="activeForm">Writing ADR 0003

content.subject: M5.1 — App Group storage with migration
content.description:
Add the app group entitlement to the app target and the widget extension. Move KnownRobots off UserDefaults.standard onto the shared suite (KnownRobot already takes a UserDefaults through its initialiser). Migrate existing entries on first run so a user's known robots are not lost on update.</description>
<parameter name="activeForm">Wiring the App Group

content.subject: M5.2 — robot snapshot the widget can read
content.description:
A widget extension lives for seconds and cannot hold the state WebSocket or a WebRTC session, so it renders a snapshot the app writes into the App Group: robot name, awake/asleep, running app, and the time it was taken. Staleness must be explicit — a widget confidently showing "awake" for a robot that is off is worse than one saying it has no fresh data.</description>
<parameter name="activeForm">Building the widget snapshot

content.subject: M5.3 — widget extension and deep links
content.description:
New iOS-only widget extension target in Apps/Project.swift (no macOS per the user's decision), timeline provider over the snapshot, small and medium families. Tapping opens the right tab, which needs onOpenURL handling in ReachyRootView — none exists yet.</description>
<parameter name="activeForm">Building the widget extension

content.subject: M5.4 — App Intents over the local network
content.description:
Wake, sleep and start-app intents that reach the robot over plain HTTP on the LAN. Remote actions through the relay are explicitly out of scope (user's decision): a WebRTC session cannot be negotiated inside an intent's deadline. Out of network the intent must fail with something a user can act on. Local Network permission in an extension is its own process and must be verified on device, not assumed.</description>
<parameter name="activeForm">Building the App Intents

content.subject: M5.5 — previews and recorded references for the widget
content.description:
Project rule 8: every state a user can land in gets a preview and a recorded reference — no robot known, asleep, awake, running an app, and stale data. Widget views render through WidgetKit, so check how they fit the existing Prefire pipeline before assuming they do.</description>
<parameter name="activeForm">Covering the widget with snapshots

content.subject: M2 — ReachyKit: hf-auth surface of the daemon
content.description: Model/HFAuth.swift (HFAuthStatus, RelayStatus with unavailable + unknown, RelayRefresh with the skipped trap, CentralRobotStatusProxy, CentralRobot), Session/HFAuthClient.swift, Transport/RobotConnection+HFAuth.swift, Session/RobotSession+HFAuth.swift (cached robotHFAccount, linkRobot, unlinkRobot). HFSignInModel + HFSignInFlow with an ASWebAuthenticationSession behind a @MainActor protocol seam so the model is testable and previews open nothing.

content.subject: M7 — Central relay client (SSE + POST)
content.description: Sources/ReachyKit/Central/CentralRelayClient.swift: GET /events read with URLSession.bytes, only data: lines decoded, POST /send whose reply body may itself be a signaling message, Bearer from an injected token provider, 60 s read timeout and 5→60 s backoff mirroring the robot's own relay, GET /api/robot-status for the robot list.

content.subject: M8.1 — RemoteControlChannel зелёный
content.description: Довести Tests/ReachyKitTests/RemoteControlChannelTests.swift до зелёного прогона (7 тестов), затем закоммитить Sources/ReachyKit/Central/RemoteControlChannel.swift. Прогон строго последовательный, один процесс SwiftPM за раз.

content.subject: M8.2 — RemoteRobotConnection поверх data-канала
content.description: Тип, реализующий RobotAPIClient через RemoteControlChannel. Карта команд проверена по исходникам даемона: handshake = get_version + get_hardware_id, daemonStatus/probeBackendReady = daemon_status, wake_up, goto_sleep, set_motor_mode, get_volume/set_volume, get_microphone_volume/set_microphone_volume, play_sound. Остальное наследует throwing-дефолты протокола — stop_sound, listMoves, playMove, urdf, kinematicsInfo, setRobotName в канале отсутствуют. ПОПРАВКА к плану: канала "pose" не существует, телеметрия идёт broadcast-ами по тому же каналу "data" и поля seq в ней нет — вместо дедупликации нужно прореживание потока 50 Гц.

content.subject: M8.3 — RemoteDataChannel поверх RTCDataChannel

Сейчас connect привязан к адресу: KnownRobots.lastAddress, стрим состояния /api/state/ws/full, viewportAddress. У удалённой сессии адреса нет, телеметрия идёт broadcast-ами по data-каналу. content.subject: Verify the whole branch before starting M5
content.description:
Five axes, one process at a time: SwiftLint strict, format-check (hk), full swift test, ReachySpike app target, snapshot references. Plus two runtime checks the automated axes cannot give: SimulatorIntegrationTests against a live sim-daemon (guards the RobotSession connect-path refactor from M9b), and a real device build/install/launch on the iPhone 17 Pro.</description>

content.subject: ADR 0003 — remote access over the Hugging Face relay
content.description:
Record the decisions already shipped and verified: HF as this app's own account (public OAuth client + PKCE, token in Keychain, live sign-in confirmed on device), the central relay as SSE + POST, the WebRTC data channel as the remote control surface, reply correlation on a wire with no request ids, assembled DaemonStatus, and what the remote path deliberately cannot do (3D scene, /wifi, /update, rename).</description>
<parameter name="activeForm">Writing ADR 0003

content.subject: M5.1 — App Group storage with migration
content.description:
Add the app group entitlement to the app target and the widget extension. Move KnownRobots off UserDefaults.standard onto the shared suite (KnownRobot already takes a UserDefaults through its initialiser). Migrate existing entries on first run so a user's known robots are not lost on update.</description>
<parameter name="activeForm">Wiring the App Group

content.subject: M5.2 — robot snapshot the widget can read
content.description:
A widget extension lives for seconds and cannot hold the state WebSocket or a WebRTC session, so it renders a snapshot the app writes into the App Group: robot name, awake/asleep, running app, and the time it was taken. Staleness must be explicit — a widget confidently showing "awake" for a robot that is off is worse than one saying it has no fresh data.</description>
<parameter name="activeForm">Building the widget snapshot

content.subject: M5.3 — widget extension and deep links
content.description:
New iOS-only widget extension target in Apps/Project.swift (no macOS per the user's decision), timeline provider over the snapshot, small and medium families. Tapping opens the right tab, which needs onOpenURL handling in ReachyRootView — none exists yet.</description>
<parameter name="activeForm">Building the widget extension

content.subject: M5.4 — App Intents over the local network
content.description:
Wake, sleep and start-app intents that reach the robot over plain HTTP on the LAN. Remote actions through the relay are explicitly out of scope (user's decision): a WebRTC session cannot be negotiated inside an intent's deadline. Out of network the intent must fail with something a user can act on. Local Network permission in an extension is its own process and must be verified on device, not assumed.</description>
<parameter name="activeForm">Building the App Intents

content.subject: M5.5 — previews and recorded references for the widget
content.description:
Project rule 8: every state a user can land in gets a preview and a recorded reference — no robot known, asleep, awake, running an app, and stale data. Widget views render through WidgetKit, so check how they fit the existing Prefire pipeline before assuming they do.</description>

content.content:
# ReachyUI

Shared SwiftUI views for all platforms (macOS/iPadOS/iOS). Depends on ReachyKit and ReachyMedia (WebRTC camera).

- Adaptive layouts, not per-platform copies; `#if os(iOS)` only for platform-exclusive APIs (Settings deep link etc.).
- `horizontalSizeClass` is unavailable on macOS — guard size-class branching with `#if os(macOS)` (always regular there).
- All robot interaction goes through `RobotSession` / `RobotBrowser` from ReachyKit — no direct URLSession here.
- Screen logic belongs in a `@MainActor @Observable` model beside the view (`MovesModel`, `LogConsoleModel`), covered
  by `Tests/ReachyUITests`; the view stays thin. `@Observable` does honour `didSet`, so derived caches can live there.
- `Section` has no title-plus-footer overload: `Section("X") { … } footer: { … }` fails to compile with a misleading
  "generic parameter 'Content' could not be inferred". Either `Section("X") { … }` or the full
  `Section { … } header: { Text("X") } footer: { … }`.
- A container view taking a closure argument _and_ two trailing `@ViewBuilder`s trips SwiftLint's
  `multiple_closures_with_trailing_closure`. Pass the extra behaviour as a child view instead
  (`OnboardingBackButton`), not as a third closure.
- `background(_:)` defaults to `ignoresSafeAreaEdges: .all`, so a full-bleed backdrop also paints the inset the
  floating tab bar sits in — bottom on iPhone, top on iPad. That bar is glass and renders whatever it finds there, so
  it turns dark on that one tab, a frame behind the switch. State the edges (`ViewportView.backdropEdges`); bleed
  upwards only where a bar pinned to match is waiting for it (`darkTitleBar()`).
- Deployment floor is iOS 18 / macOS 15 (`Package.swift`, `Apps/Project.swift`), set by `RealityView`.
  `ScrollPosition`, `onScrollPhaseChange` and `onScrollGeometryChange` are available; the zero-height sentinel row in
  `LogConsoleScreen` predates the bump and is not a required pattern.

## Previews and snapshots

`Previews/` sits here but is **excluded from the SwiftPM target** (`Package.swift`) and compiled only by the Xcode
targets in `Apps/`. `#Preview` is an external macro implemented by `libPreviewsMacros.dylib`, which ships inside
Xcode's platform SDKs and not in the pinned swift.org toolchain — a `#Preview` anywhere under a SwiftPM target breaks
`mise run build`, `mise run test` and CI with "plugin for module 'PreviewsMacros' not found".

Adding a screen (project rule 8) means: a preview per state in `Previews/<Screen>Previews.swift`, whatever seam and
`#if DEBUG` factory those states need, `mise run test:snapshots:record`, and `git add` on the PNGs.

- Preview files use `@testable import ReachyUI`; that is why `ENABLE_TESTABILITY` is set for the whole Xcode project.
- **Prefire reads previews off the filesystem; Xcode compiles the file list Tuist baked in.** A new file under
  `Previews/` is therefore picked up by the generator but not compiled until `mise run project` runs again — which is
  why the snapshot tasks depend on it. A bare `xcodebuild` skips that and fails with "cannot find … in scope".
- Anything a preview body references must be visible target-wide, because Prefire copies the body into a separate
  generated file. Shared wrappers live in `PreviewScene`; a `private` helper compiles locally and breaks the test.
- **A preview with no `traits:` is captured at full device size.** Prefire defaults the trait list to `.device`
  (`RawPreviewModel.isScreen`), and that device trait is what carries `horizontalSizeClass` — so it is what makes the
  iPad snapshot exercise the regular-width layout. Components opt out with `traits: .sizeThatFitsLayout`.
- **A preview must be final on its first frame.** Prefire captures synchronously and its `.snapshot(delay:)` modifier
  lives in a module this target cannot import without breaking the macOS build. Never rely on a `.task` completing —
  hand the view a model that is already in its end state (`AudioSettingsModel.preview()`, `RobotSession.preview()`).
- Model preview factories live **in the model's own file** under `#if DEBUG`, not in `Previews/`: they write members
  that are `private` to that file, and `@testable` does not reach `private`.
- Screens take their model through an initialiser with a default (`init(session:model:)`), so production call sites
  are unchanged and previews inject a frozen one.
- A defaulted argument whose value is `@MainActor` (`= SpikeModel()`, `= .preview()`) compiles in the SwiftPM targets
  but not in the `Apps/` ones, where it is evaluated nonisolated. Use `nil` and resolve it in the body.
- A model that already takes a factory closure (`OnboardingModel(session:)`, `BLEConsoleModel(link:)`) needs no new
  seam — hand it a `BLELink.preview(…)`, which sits on an inert `PreviewBLETransport` and is assigned its state
  directly. Building the link is not enough on its own: `OnboardingModel.session` is only set by `beginScan()`, which
  is the CoreBluetooth call a preview must not make, so the factory assigns it.
- A screen whose `.task` guards on `model == nil` needs no `reachyPreviewMode` check — injecting the model is what
  makes it inert. Add the guard only where the effect runs unconditionally (`WiFiSettingsCard`, `LogConsoleScreen`).
- Not covered, deliberately: `SceneViewport` in `.ready` (a bare `RealityView`) and `CameraViewport` in `.streaming`
  (Metal-backed `RTCMTLVideoView`). Neither renders anything meaningful headless — snapshot their overlay phases.
- One `RobotSceneModel` per preview: `ReachyScene/AGENTS.md` requires exactly one live `RealityView` per model.
- **Navigation chrome does not stay inside a preview card.** SwiftUI hoists `.toolbar` and
  `.searchable` out of the storybook's scaled cards into the app's own bars, even though each
  preview brings its own `NavigationStack` — this is the limitation Prefire records as
  "NavigationView in Preview not supported for Playbook". The storybook hides its root bars to
  absorb it; `LogConsoleScreen`'s search field still floats over the catalogue, which is cosmetic
  and not worth contorting the screen for. Snapshots are unaffected — they capture the title _and_
  the toolbar items, so `RobotScreen`'s Settings gear and `MovesScreen`'s Refresh are covered.
  Only the storybook hoists.

Five axes, one process at a time: SwiftLint strict, format-check (hk), full swift test, ReachySpike app target, snapshot references. Plus two runtime checks the automated axes cannot give: SimulatorIntegrationTests against a live sim-daemon (guards the RobotSession connect-path refactor from M9b), and a real device build/install/launch on the iPhone 17 Pro.</description>

content.subject: ADR 0003 — remote access over the Hugging Face relay
content.description:
Record the decisions already shipped and verified: HF as this app's own account (public OAuth client + PKCE, token in Keychain, live sign-in confirmed on device), the central relay as SSE + POST, the WebRTC data channel as the remote control surface, reply correlation on a wire with no request ids, assembled DaemonStatus, and what the remote path deliberately cannot do (3D scene, /wifi, /update, rename).</description>
<parameter name="activeForm">Writing ADR 0003

content.subject: M5.1 — App Group storage with migration
content.description:
Add the app group entitlement to the app target and the widget extension. Move KnownRobots off UserDefaults.standard onto the shared suite (KnownRobot already takes a UserDefaults through its initialiser). Migrate existing entries on first run so a user's known robots are not lost on update.</description>
<parameter name="activeForm">Wiring the App Group

content.subject: M5.2 — robot snapshot the widget can read
content.description:
A widget extension lives for seconds and cannot hold the state WebSocket or a WebRTC session, so it renders a snapshot the app writes into the App Group: robot name, awake/asleep, running app, and the time it was taken. Staleness must be explicit — a widget confidently showing "awake" for a robot that is off is worse than one saying it has no fresh data.</description>
<parameter name="activeForm">Building the widget snapshot

content.subject: M5.3 — widget extension and deep links
content.description:
New iOS-only widget extension target in Apps/Project.swift (no macOS per the user's decision), timeline provider over the snapshot, small and medium families. Tapping opens the right tab, which needs onOpenURL handling in ReachyRootView — none exists yet.</description>
<parameter name="activeForm">Building the widget extension

content.subject: M5.4 — App Intents over the local network
content.description:
Wake, sleep and start-app intents that reach the robot over plain HTTP on the LAN. Remote actions through the relay are explicitly out of scope (user's decision): a WebRTC session cannot be negotiated inside an intent's deadline. Out of network the intent must fail with something a user can act on. Local Network permission in an extension is its own process and must be verified on device, not assumed.</description>
<parameter name="activeForm">Building the App Intents

content.subject: M5.5 — previews and recorded references for the widget
content.description:
Project rule 8: every state a user can land in gets a preview and a recorded reference — no robot known, asleep, awake, running an app, and stale data. Widget views render through WidgetKit, so check how they fit the existing Prefire pipeline before assuming they do.</description>

content.subject: M4.5 — Previews and recorded snapshots
content.description: Project rule 8: a preview per state (store loading/empty/catalogue/installed+running/offline; overlay installing/failed/success), then mise run test:snapshots, then record, then an explicit git add of the LFS PNGs.

content.subject: M6 — Hugging Face account card and sign-in flow
content.description: Sources/ReachyUI/Settings/HFAccountSection.swift (WiFiSettingsCard template): signed-out with one-tap sign-in plus a paste-token fallback, signed-in with username and avatar, this robot's link state and relay status, Sign out. HFSignInModel + HFSignInFlow with an ASWebAuthenticationSession behind a @MainActor protocol seam so the model is testable and previews open nothing.
content.activeForm: Building the Hugging Face account UI

content.subject: M7 — Central relay client (SSE + POST)
content.description: Sources/ReachyKit/Central/CentralRelayClient.swift: GET /events read with URLSession.bytes, only data: lines decoded, POST /send whose reply body may itself be a signaling message, Bearer from an injected token provider, 60 s read timeout and 5→60 s backoff mirroring the robot's own relay, GET /api/robot-status for the robot list.

content.subject: M8.1 — RemoteControlChannel зелёный
content.description: Довести Tests/ReachyKitTests/RemoteControlChannelTests.swift до зелёного прогона (7 тестов), затем закоммитить Sources/ReachyKit/Central/RemoteControlChannel.swift. Прогон строго последовательный, один процесс SwiftPM за раз.

content.subject: M8.2 — RemoteRobotConnection поверх data-канала
content.description: Тип, реализующий RobotAPIClient через RemoteControlChannel. Карта команд проверена по исходникам даемона: handshake = get_version + get_hardware_id, daemonStatus/probeBackendReady = daemon_status, wake_up, goto_sleep, set_motor_mode, get_volume/set_volume, get_microphone_volume/set_microphone_volume, play_sound. Остальное наследует throwing-дефолты протокола — stop_sound, listMoves, playMove, urdf, kinematicsInfo, setRobotName в канале отсутствуют. ПОПРАВКА к плану: канала "pose" не существует, телеметрия идёт broadcast-ами по тому же каналу "data" и поля seq в ней нет — вместо дедупликации нужно прореживание потока 50 Гц.

content.subject: M8.3 — RemoteDataChannel поверх RTCDataChannel
content.description: В ReachyMedia: реализация RemoteDataChannel на RTCDataChannel. CameraSession.swift:305 peerConnection(_:didOpen:) сейчас пустышка. Робот открывает ровно ОДИН канал с меткой "data" (media_server.py:1712) — второго канала нет, ловить надо его.

content.subject: M9 — экран «Your Reachies» и удалённое подключение
content.description: ReachyUI: список роботов из central, степпер LINK → SESSION → WAKE-UP, обработка отказов через RemoteSessionEnd. Плюс превью и записанные снапшоты по правилу 8.

content.subject: M5 — виджеты (App Group, App Intents, extension)
content.description: Общий App Group для состояния робота, App Intents для команд, target виджет-расширения в Apps/Project.swift. Независимо от M8/M9.

content.subject: M10 — документация
content.description: ADR-0003 про удалённый доступ, docs/research/central-relay.md, обновление .claude/rules/, README. Плюс уже накопленные заметки в AGENTS.md.

content.subject: M9b — RobotSession без адреса, удалённое подключение
content.description: RobotSession.connect(using:) с готовым клиентом вместо makeClient(address). Сейчас connect привязан к адресу: KnownRobots.lastAddress, стрим состояния /api/state/ws/full, viewportAddress. У удалённой сессии адреса нет, телеметрия идёт broadcast-ами по data-каналу. Плюс сборка цепочки CentralSignalingTransport → CameraSession → WebRTCDataChannel → RemoteRobotConnection.

content.subject: Verify the whole branch before starting M5
content.description:
Five axes, one process at a time: SwiftLint strict, format-check (hk), full swift test, ReachySpike app target, snapshot references. Plus two runtime checks the automated axes cannot give: SimulatorIntegrationTests against a live sim-daemon (guards the RobotSession connect-path refactor from M9b), and a real device build/install/launch on the iPhone 17 Pro.</description>
<parameter name="activeForm">Verifying the branch before M5

content.subject: ADR 0003 — remote access over the Hugging Face relay
content.description:
Record the decisions already shipped and verified: HF as this app's own account (public OAuth client + PKCE, token in Keychain, live sign-in confirmed on device), the central relay as SSE + POST, the WebRTC data channel as the remote control surface, reply correlation on a wire with no request ids, assembled DaemonStatus, and what the remote path deliberately cannot do (3D scene, /wifi, /update, rename).</description>
<parameter name="activeForm">Writing ADR 0003

content.subject: M5.1 — App Group storage with migration
content.description:
Add the app group entitlement to the app target and the widget extension. Move KnownRobots off UserDefaults.standard onto the shared suite (KnownRobot already takes a UserDefaults through its initialiser). Migrate existing entries on first run so a user's known robots are not lost on update.</description>
<parameter name="activeForm">Wiring the App Group

content.subject: M5.2 — robot snapshot the widget can read
content.description:
A widget extension lives for seconds and cannot hold the state WebSocket or a WebRTC session, so it renders a snapshot the app writes into the App Group: robot name, awake/asleep, running app, and the time it was taken. Staleness must be explicit — a widget confidently showing "awake" for a robot that is off is worse than one saying it has no fresh data.</description>
<parameter name="activeForm">Building the widget snapshot

content.subject: M5.3 — widget extension and deep links
content.description:
New iOS-only widget extension target in Apps/Project.swift (no macOS per the user's decision), timeline provider over the snapshot, small and medium families. Tapping opens the right tab, which needs onOpenURL handling in ReachyRootView — none exists yet.</description>
<parameter name="activeForm">Building the widget extension

content.subject: M5.4 — App Intents over the local network
content.description:
Wake, sleep and start-app intents that reach the robot over plain HTTP on the LAN. Remote actions through the relay are explicitly out of scope (user's decision): a WebRTC session cannot be negotiated inside an intent's deadline. Out of network the intent must fail with something a user can act on. Local Network permission in an extension is its own process and must be verified on device, not assumed.</description>
<parameter name="activeForm">Building the App Intents

content.subject: M5.5 — previews and recorded references for the widget
content.description:
Project rule 8: every state a user can land in gets a preview and a recorded reference — no robot known, asleep, awake, running an app, and stale data. Widget views render through WidgetKit, so check how they fit the existing Prefire pipeline before assuming they do.</description>
<parameter name="activeForm">Covering the widget with snapshots

Five axes, one process at a time: SwiftLint strict, format-check (hk), full swift test, ReachySpike app target, snapshot references. Plus two runtime checks the automated axes cannot give: SimulatorIntegrationTests against a live sim-daemon (guards the RobotSession connect-path refactor from M9b), and a real device build/install/launch on the iPhone 17 Pro.</description>

content.subject: ADR 0003 — remote access over the Hugging Face relay
content.description:
Record the decisions already shipped and verified: HF as this app's own account (public OAuth client + PKCE, token in Keychain, live sign-in confirmed on device), the central relay as SSE + POST, the WebRTC data channel as the remote control surface, reply correlation on a wire with no request ids, assembled DaemonStatus, and what the remote path deliberately cannot do (3D scene, /wifi, /update, rename).</description>
<parameter name="activeForm">Writing ADR 0003

content.subject: M5.1 — App Group storage with migration
content.description:
Add the app group entitlement to the app target and the widget extension. Move KnownRobots off UserDefaults.standard onto the shared suite (KnownRobot already takes a UserDefaults through its initialiser). Migrate existing entries on first run so a user's known robots are not lost on update.</description>
<parameter name="activeForm">Wiring the App Group

content.subject: M5.2 — robot snapshot the widget can read
content.description:
A widget extension lives for seconds and cannot hold the state WebSocket or a WebRTC session, so it renders a snapshot the app writes into the App Group: robot name, awake/asleep, running app, and the time it was taken. Staleness must be explicit — a widget confidently showing "awake" for a robot that is off is worse than one saying it has no fresh data.</description>
<parameter name="activeForm">Building the widget snapshot

content.subject: M5.3 — widget extension and deep links
content.description:
New iOS-only widget extension target in Apps/Project.swift (no macOS per the user's decision), timeline provider over the snapshot, small and medium families. Tapping opens the right tab, which needs onOpenURL handling in ReachyRootView — none exists yet.</description>
<parameter name="activeForm">Building the widget extension

content.subject: M5.4 — App Intents over the local network
content.description:
Wake, sleep and start-app intents that reach the robot over plain HTTP on the LAN. Remote actions through the relay are explicitly out of scope (user's decision): a WebRTC session cannot be negotiated inside an intent's deadline. Out of network the intent must fail with something a user can act on. Local Network permission in an extension is its own process and must be verified on device, not assumed.</description>
<parameter name="activeForm">Building the App Intents

content.subject: M5.5 — previews and recorded references for the widget
content.description:
Project rule 8: every state a user can land in gets a preview and a recorded reference — no robot known, asleep, awake, running an app, and stale data. Widget views render through WidgetKit, so check how they fit the existing Prefire pipeline before assuming they do.</description>

Add the app group entitlement to the app target and the widget extension. content.subject: M5.2 — robot snapshot the widget can read
content.description:
A widget extension lives for seconds and cannot hold the state WebSocket or a WebRTC session, so it renders a snapshot the app writes into the App Group: robot name, awake/asleep, running app, and the time it was taken. Staleness must be explicit — a widget confidently showing "awake" for a robot that is off is worse than one saying it has no fresh data.</description>

content.description:

content.subject: M5.4 — App Intents over the local network
content.description:
Wake, sleep and start-app intents that reach the robot over plain HTTP on the LAN. Remote actions through the relay are explicitly out of scope (user's decision): a WebRTC session cannot be negotiated inside an intent's deadline. Out of network the intent must fail with something a user can act on. Local Network permission in an extension is its own process and must be verified on device, not assumed.</description>

content.thinking:
The wake/sleep logic is tightly coupled to RobotSession, which makes it awkward for intents since they need to spin up the session, establish the connection with all its handshakes and polling, and do it all within the intent's time constraints. A better approach would be to extract this sequence into a reusable component that works directly with RobotAPIClient, bypassing the session layer entirely.

I'm sketching out a RobotPower type that encapsulates both power transitions independently of any session — this avoids duplicating the logic between the intent and the session, which is the real risk here. Rather than having two separate implementations that could drift apart, I'll refactor RobotSession to use this shared component internally, so there's only one source of truth for how power commands work.

The session layer will handle the backend-not-running case (checking status and triggering runBackendStart if needed), while RobotPower stays focused purely on the protocol sequence. I'll start with a test-driven approach and check what configuration fields I actually need — motorSettleDelay, movePollInterval, moveTimeout — before diving into the implementation.

content.subject: ADR 0003 — remote access over the Hugging Face relay
content.description:
Record the decisions already shipped and verified: HF as this app's own account (public OAuth client + PKCE, token in Keychain, live sign-in confirmed on device), the central relay as SSE + POST, the WebRTC data channel as the remote control surface, reply correlation on a wire with no request ids, assembled DaemonStatus, and what the remote path deliberately cannot do (3D scene, /wifi, /update, rename).</description>
<parameter name="activeForm">Writing ADR 0003

content.subject: M5.1 — App Group storage with migration
content.description:
Add the app group entitlement to the app target and the widget extension. Move KnownRobots off UserDefaults.standard onto the shared suite (KnownRobot already takes a UserDefaults through its initialiser). Migrate existing entries on first run so a user's known robots are not lost on update.</description>
<parameter name="activeForm">Wiring the App Group

content.subject: M5.2 — robot snapshot the widget can read
content.description:
A widget extension lives for seconds and cannot hold the state WebSocket or a WebRTC session, so it renders a snapshot the app writes into the App Group: robot name, awake/asleep, running app, and the time it was taken. Staleness must be explicit — a widget confidently showing "awake" for a robot that is off is worse than one saying it has no fresh data.</description>
<parameter name="activeForm">Building the widget snapshot

content.subject: M5.3 — widget extension and deep links
content.description:
New iOS-only widget extension target in Apps/Project.swift (no macOS per the user's decision), timeline provider over the snapshot, small and medium families. Tapping opens the right tab, which needs onOpenURL handling in ReachyRootView — none exists yet.</description>
<parameter name="activeForm">Building the widget extension

content.subject: M5.4 — App Intents over the local network
content.description:
Wake, sleep and start-app intents that reach the robot over plain HTTP on the LAN. Remote actions through the relay are explicitly out of scope (user's decision): a WebRTC session cannot be negotiated inside an intent's deadline. Out of network the intent must fail with something a user can act on. Local Network permission in an extension is its own process and must be verified on device, not assumed.</description>
<parameter name="activeForm">Building the App Intents

content.subject: M5.5 — previews and recorded references for the widget
content.description:
Project rule 8: every state a user can land in gets a preview and a recorded reference — no robot known, asleep, awake, running an app, and stale data. Widget views render through WidgetKit, so check how they fit the existing Prefire pipeline before assuming they do.</description>

content.subject: M8.2 — RemoteRobotConnection поверх data-канала
content.description: Тип, реализующий RobotAPIClient через RemoteControlChannel. Карта команд проверена по исходникам даемона: handshake = get_version + get_hardware_id, daemonStatus/probeBackendReady = daemon_status, wake_up, goto_sleep, set_motor_mode, get_volume/set_volume, get_microphone_volume/set_microphone_volume, play_sound. content.subject: Verify the whole branch before starting M5
content.description:
Five axes, one process at a time: SwiftLint strict, format-check (hk), full swift test, ReachySpike app target, snapshot references. Plus two runtime checks the automated axes cannot give: SimulatorIntegrationTests against a live sim-daemon (guards the RobotSession connect-path refactor from M9b), and a real device build/install/launch on the iPhone 17 Pro.</description>
<parameter name="activeForm">Verifying the branch before M5

content.subject: ADR 0003 — remote access over the Hugging Face relay
content.description:
Record the decisions already shipped and verified: HF as this app's own account (public OAuth client + PKCE, token in Keychain, live sign-in confirmed on device), the central relay as SSE + POST, the WebRTC data channel as the remote control surface, reply correlation on a wire with no request ids, assembled DaemonStatus, and what the remote path deliberately cannot do (3D scene, /wifi, /update, rename).</description>
<parameter name="activeForm">Writing ADR 0003

content.subject: M5.1 — App Group storage with migration
content.description:
Add the app group entitlement to the app target and the widget extension. Move KnownRobots off UserDefaults.standard onto the shared suite (KnownRobot already takes a UserDefaults through its initialiser). Migrate existing entries on first run so a user's known robots are not lost on update.</description>
<parameter name="activeForm">Wiring the App Group

content.subject: M5.2 — robot snapshot the widget can read
content.description:
A widget extension lives for seconds and cannot hold the state WebSocket or a WebRTC session, so it renders a snapshot the app writes into the App Group: robot name, awake/asleep, running app, and the time it was taken. Staleness must be explicit — a widget confidently showing "awake" for a robot that is off is worse than one saying it has no fresh data.</description>
<parameter name="activeForm">Building the widget snapshot

content.subject: M5.3 — widget extension and deep links
content.description:
New iOS-only widget extension target in Apps/Project.swift (no macOS per the user's decision), timeline provider over the snapshot, small and medium families. Tapping opens the right tab, which needs onOpenURL handling in ReachyRootView — none exists yet.</description>
<parameter name="activeForm">Building the widget extension

content.subject: M5.4 — App Intents over the local network
content.description:
Wake, sleep and start-app intents that reach the robot over plain HTTP on the LAN. Remote actions through the relay are explicitly out of scope (user's decision): a WebRTC session cannot be negotiated inside an intent's deadline. Out of network the intent must fail with something a user can act on. Local Network permission in an extension is its own process and must be verified on device, not assumed.</description>
<parameter name="activeForm">Building the App Intents

content.subject: M5.5 — previews and recorded references for the widget
content.description:
Project rule 8: every state a user can land in gets a preview and a recorded reference — no robot known, asleep, awake, running an app, and stale data. Widget views render through WidgetKit, so check how they fit the existing Prefire pipeline before assuming they do.</description>
<parameter name="activeForm">Covering the widget with snapshots

M5 реализован. Итог по коммитам в worktree `widgets-m5`:

| Коммит | Что |
|---|---|
| `a090d84` | ADR 0003 + README |

| `9c2c042` | App Intents (Shortcuts/Siri) |

**575 тестов**, **192 снапшота**, линт `0 violations` на 1120 файлах, macOS-сборка и симулятор — чисто.

## Решения, которые стоит знать

**Виджет не может ничего спросить у робота** — расширение живёт секунды. Поэтому оно рендерит снимок, который пишет приложение, а снимок несёт время съёмки. Отсюда главное: таймлайн отдаёт **две** записи — что верно сейчас и момент, когда чтение перестаёт быть достоверным. Без второй виджет вечно показывал бы «Awake» у робота, выключенного час назад: приложение не работает, чтобы это заметить.

**Виды виджета — отдельный `ReachyWidgetUI`, не `ReachyUI`.** Последний линкует WebRTC и RealityKit; тащить медиастек в процесс с жёстким лимитом памяти ради двух строк текста нельзя.

**Последовательность wake/sleep вынесена в `RobotPower`** и теперь общая для приложения и интента — иначе порядок жил бы в двух копиях. Порядок здесь не деталь: если снять питание до конца анимации сна, голова падает. На это есть отдельные тесты.

**Интенты — только локальная сеть**, как вы и решили. Вне сети падают сразу с внятным текстом, а не висят до таймаута.

## Что нужно от вас — то же, что и в первый раз

Расширение имеет **свой** bundle id, и его App ID тоже требует App Groups:

```bash
open Apps/ReachyMiniApps.xcworkspace
```

Таргет **ReachyWidget** → Signing & Capabilities → + Capability → App Groups → `group.com.alexey1312.ReachyMini`.

## Непроверенное, прямо

- **Виджет ни разу не работал на устройстве** — сборка блокирована подписью выше. Симулятор компилирует расширение чисто, но это доказывает компиляцию, а не поведение таймлайна.
- **Local Network permission у расширения не проверялось.** Это отдельный процесс; интенты я пометил как требующие проверки на железе именно из-за этого.
- **Control Widget (iOS 18)** из состава M5 не делал — в списке он был, но без явного вашего решения я не стал добавлять ещё одну поверхность.

Как добавите capability — соберу, установлю и проверю виджет на телефоне.

```
`build` / `test` are SwiftPM only — they never compile `Apps/ReachySpike`. Use `build:app` for that; CI runs it as a
separate job, so app-target breakage no longer reaches `main` unnoticed.
`test:filter` matches type names (`RobotSessionAudioTests`), not `@Suite` display names.
`SimulatorIntegrationTests` is gated on `REACHY_SIM_HOST`, so plain `test` **skips it silently and reports green** —
run `test:sim` against a live `sim-daemon` to exercise it.
`swift test --skip-build` runs the previously built binary: rebuild with `swift build --build-tests` after editing a
test, or the run silently verifies stale code.
Everything pipes through xcsift, which on long runs can truncate and report `status: incomplete` while hiding the real
result — verify the artifact, or rerun the tool directly
```

Для новой директории превью нужны три отдельных правки: обновить `sources` в `Apps/.prefire.yml`, затем то же самое в обоих целевых объектах в `Project.swift`, и добавить `testable_imports` для модулей, которые превью импортируют — пропустить первый шаг означает, что превью скомпилируются, но тестов не сгенерируется.

App Group — это не подстановочная возможность, каждый целевой объект, который её объявляет (приложение и расширение виджета отдельно), должен иметь свой App ID, созданный через Signing & Capabilities в Xcode, потому что `xcodebuild -allowProvisioningUpdates` из CLI не может это сделать.

`Task` внутри актора наследует его изоляцию, поэтому `await self.foo()` на изолированном методе — это холостой вызов, на который компилятор выдаст предупреждение, и то же самое происходит, когда один `static func` становится `nonisolated` — это каскадирует на всё, что он вызывает.

`UserDefaults` не Sendable — мелочь, но появится снова при работе с App Group. Выбираю пять самых ценных пунктов: инкрементальная сборка и warnings, exit code и бесконечные процессы, проблема с test:sim из-за среды, .prefire.yml для новой директории превью, и явный App ID для App Groups при добавлении расширений.

content.text:
Control Widget готов — две кнопки в Пункте управления, коммит `9d583fc`. 575 тестов, линт чистый.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
Кнопки, а не переключатель: toggle обязан знать текущее состояние робота, чтобы себя нарисовать, — а этот процесс спросить не может. Он отрисовал бы догадку из снимка и опроверг бы сам себя, как только та протухнет.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

Теперь возвращаюсь к разбору сессии. Вот что стоит записать — только повторяемое.

### Update: ./CLAUDE.md

**Why:** «0 warnings» на инкрементальной сборке ничего не доказывает — я на этом потерял время и сначала выдвинул неверную гипотезу про расхождение тулчейнов.

```diff
+ **A green `warnings: 0` proves nothing on an incremental build** — the compiler emits diagnostics only for files it
+ actually recompiles, so a 20-second `mise run test` stays silent about code it did not touch. Five warnings in
+ freshly written files surfaced only when a device build compiled the tree from scratch. `touch` the sources and
+ rebuild the target before believing a clean run.
```

### Update: ./CLAUDE.md

**Why:** дважды за сессию `| tail` соврал — сначала спрятал лог демона, потом проглотил падение `test:sim`.

```diff
  through `tail`. A run that timed out in your tool keeps running and keeps the lock, and every later command then
  looks like the code under test is hanging. Check `pgrep -f 'swift-build|swift-test|swift-frontend'` before
  diagnosing a hang, and run one SwiftPM process at a time.
+ Piping a task through `tail` also swallows its exit status (`set -o pipefail` is inside the task, not your shell)
+ and shows **nothing at all** for a process that never exits — `mise run sim-daemon | tail` looks like a dead daemon.
+ Redirect to a file and read that instead.
```

### Update: ./CLAUDE.md

**Why:** `test:sim` сейчас не может быть зелёным целиком, и это среда, а не код — час отладки на ровном месте.

```diff
  `SimulatorIntegrationTests` is gated on `REACHY_SIM_HOST`, so plain `test` **skips it silently and reports green** —
  run `test:sim` against a live `sim-daemon` to exercise it.
+ `test:sim` currently passes 6 of 7: the webrtc-signalling test times out because `.venv-sim`'s GStreamer fails its
+ plugin scan, so webrtcsink never registers a producer (`No caps found for stream audio_0` in the daemon log, logged
+ *before* any client connects — check the timestamps before blaming the client).
```

### Update: ./CLAUDE.md

**Why:** новая директория превью компилируется и молча не порождает ни одного теста — Prefire читает собственный список путей.

```diff
+ A new *directory* of previews needs three edits, not one: `sources` in `Apps/.prefire.yml` (Prefire reads its own
+ list, not the target's), the `sources` of **both** preview-hosting targets in `Project.swift`, and `testable_imports`
+ for any module those previews name — Prefire's generated file imports that list and nothing else. Miss the first and
+ the previews compile while generating no tests at all.
```

### Update: ./CLAUDE.md

**Why:** повторится для любого следующего расширения; из CLI это не чинится.

```diff
+ **An App Group is not a wildcard capability.** `iOS Team Provisioning Profile: *` cannot carry it, so every target
+ that declares one — the app and each extension separately, each with its own App ID — needs it added once through
+ Xcode's Signing & Capabilities. `xcodebuild -allowProvisioningUpdates` reports `No Accounts` and cannot create it.
```

### Update: ./CLAUDE.md

**Why:** таблица модулей устарела — появился `ReachyWidgetUI`, и причина его существования неочевидна.

```diff
- | Packages | `ReachyKit` (transport + domain) → `ReachyMedia` (WebRTC) / `ReachyScene` (RealityKit) → `ReachyUI` → `Apps/` |
```

1	# ReachyMini — Agent Instructions
2	
3	Native Swift client (macOS/iPadOS/iOS) for the Reachy Mini Wireless robot. Pure network client to the robot daemon's
4	HTTP/WebSocket API. Swift 6, strict concurrency.
5	
6	## Environment Setup — MANDATORY
7	
8	The development environment is installed **only** via:
9	
10	```bash
11	./bootstrap.sh
12	```
13	
14	It installs all pinned tools (swiftformat, swiftlint, hk, dprint, actionlint, git-cliff, xcsift, tuist) through the
15	self-contained `./bin/mise` binary and wires git hooks (`core.hooksPath .githooks`).
16	
17	- **Never** install tools globally (`brew install swiftlint`, `npm i -g`, etc.).
18	- **Never** call tools bare (`swift build`, `swiftlint`) — always `./bin/mise run <task>` or `./bin/mise x -- <tool>`,
19	  which guarantees pinned versions and PATH.
20	- Swift itself is managed by swiftly via `.swift-version`, not by mise.
21	- Tool versions are pinned in `mise.toml` + `mise.lock`. After editing `[tools]`: `trash mise.lock && ./bin/mise lock`.
22	  Find updates with `./bin/mise latest <tool>` — `mise outdated` reports nothing here, because an exact pin always
23	  matches its own request.
24	- The `hk` version in `mise.toml` must match the `hk@X.Y.Z` package URI in `hk.pkl` (bump together).
25	- `mise run project` (tuist generate) needs a one-time `./bin/mise x -- tuist auth login` — the project is connected
26	  to tuist.dev (`alexey1312/reachy-mini-desktop-app-swift` in `Apps/Tuist.swift`). That handle names the **tuist.dev
27	  project**, not this repository, and deliberately keeps the pre-rename name: renaming the GitHub repo does not rename
28	  the server-side project, so "fixing" it to match `reachy-mini-swift` points generation at a project that does not exist.
29	- Run every `tuist` command from `Apps/` — `Tuist.swift` lives there and tuist only searches _upward_, so from the repo
30	  root it finds no manifest and reports the project as unconnected to the server (`run 'tuist init'`).
31	- Use `mise run inspect:bundle [path]` rather than `tuist inspect bundle`: it handles the cwd, defaults to the iOS
32	  device bundle, and rejects a macOS one (which keeps `Info.plist` under `Contents/`, where the command wants it at
33	  the root). Size numbers only mean something off a Release archive — a Debug bundle carries `__preview.dylib`,
34	  `*.debug.dylib` and the provisioning profile, none of which ship.
35	- Do **not** set `enableCaching` — without a running cache daemon every compile task waits out a CAS socket deadline,
36	  and CI has neither the daemon nor cache credentials (this repo is not connected to the tuist.dev project).
37	- `Package.resolved` **oscillates between the two build systems, and neither is wrong.** `xcodebuild` resolves the
38	  whole Tuist workspace and writes back to the root package's file, adding five pins (Prefire, swift-snapshot-testing,
39	  swift-syntax, swift-custom-dump, xctest-dynamic-overlay); `swift build` / `swift test` see only the root package and
40	  strip them again. Merging a branch that predates them drops them silently too — git sees a clean delete on one side.
41	  Commit the 16-pin version (run `mise run project` or any snapshot task last), never hand-edit it, and expect the
42	  file to show as modified after a plain `mise run test`.
43	
44	## Quick Reference
45	
46	```bash
47	./bin/mise run build          # Debug build (piped through xcsift)
48	./bin/mise run build:app      # Build the ReachySpike app target (generates first)
49	./bin/mise run test           # All tests, parallel
50	./bin/mise run test:filter T  # Filter tests
51	./bin/mise run lint           # SwiftLint --strict + actionlint + hk lockstep
52	./bin/mise run format         # Format all (hk fix --all)
53	./bin/mise run format-check   # CI formatting check
54	./bin/mise run project        # tuist generate (Apps/)
55	./bin/mise run inspect:bundle # Upload an iOS bundle-size analysis to tuist.dev
56	./bin/mise run sim-daemon     # Simulated robot daemon (MuJoCo, LAN-reachable)
57	./bin/mise run test:sim       # Integration tests against a running sim-daemon
58	./bin/mise run update-spec    # Refresh + normalize daemon OpenAPI spec
59	./bin/mise run test:snapshots # Snapshot-test every ReachyUI preview (iOS Simulator)
60	./bin/mise run test:snapshots:record  # Re-record the reference images
61	./bin/mise run storybook      # Browsable catalogue of every preview, on a simulator
62	```
63	
64	`build` / `test` are SwiftPM only — they never compile `Apps/ReachySpike`. Use `build:app` for that; CI runs it as a

Готово. Итог:

## Применено три правки

Все — в `AGENTS.md` (корневой `CLAUDE.md` это симлинк на него, писать через симлинк нельзя):

- новая директория превью требует записи в `.prefire.yml`, иначе тесты молча не генерируются;
- App Group не бывает wildcard-capability — каждый таргет со своим App ID нужно один раз провести через Xcode;
- `ReachyWidgetUI` в таблице модулей, с явным запретом тянуть туда `ReachyMedia`.

Первые три предложения (инкрементальные warnings, `| tail`, `test:sim` 6/7) не записывал — как вы и сказали.

## Про Tuist — добавлять ничего не нужно

Entitlement уже объявлен в `Project.swift`, и Tuist генерирует из него файл:

```xml
<key>com.apple.security.application-groups</key>
<array><string>group.com.alexey1312.ReachyMini</string></array>
```

То, что вы сделали в Xcode, — создало App ID и группу **в аккаунте Apple**. Это не файл в репозитории, поэтому регенерация проекта его не затрёт, но и заскриптовать это нельзя.

## Control Widget добавлен

Две кнопки — «Wake up» и «Sleep» — в Пункте управления, на тех же интентах, что и Siri. Интенты переехали в `ReachyWidgetUI`, чтобы приложение и расширение использовали одни и те же, а `AppShortcutsProvider` остался в приложении: Apple берёт шорткаты только из главного бандла.

## Сборка на устройство прошла

`errors: 0, warnings: 0`, приложение с расширением установлено и запущено. Ветка `worktree-widgets-m5`:

| Коммит | Что |
|---|---|
| `a090d84` | ADR 0003 + README |
| `b0fc4fc` | App Group + миграция |
| `fd046c9` | Снимок для виджета |
| `74d0e18` | Расширение + deep links |
| `0c7e0a9` | Превью + 12 эталонов |
| `9c2c042` | App Intents |
| `9d583fc` | Control Widget |
| `d92fa0e` | Документация |

**575 тестов**, **192 снапшота**, линт `0 violations` на 1128 файлах.

## Что проверить руками — я этого сделать не могу

Виджет установлен, но **не размещён**: добавьте его на домашний экран (долгое нажатие → «+» → Reachy Mini) и кнопки в Пункт управления (Настройки → Пункт управления). Проверить стоит именно поведение снимка: подключитесь к роботу, посмотрите, что виджет показал состояние, затем оставьте телефон — через полчаса он должен сам перейти на «Last seen …» вместо «Awake».

И то, что по-прежнему не проверялось: **Local Network permission у расширения**. Интенты идут по локальной сети, а расширение — отдельный процесс со своим разрешением; поведёт ли себя это как в приложении, покажет только запуск на железе.

Five axes, one process at a time: SwiftLint strict, format-check (hk), full swift test, ReachySpike app target, snapshot references. Plus two runtime checks the automated axes cannot give: SimulatorIntegrationTests against a live sim-daemon (guards the RobotSession connect-path refactor from M9b), and a real device build/install/launch on the iPhone 17 Pro.</description>

content.subject: ADR 0003 — remote access over the Hugging Face relay
content.description:
Record the decisions already shipped and verified: HF as this app's own account (public OAuth client + PKCE, token in Keychain, live sign-in confirmed on device), the central relay as SSE + POST, the WebRTC data channel as the remote control surface, reply correlation on a wire with no request ids, assembled DaemonStatus, and what the remote path deliberately cannot do (3D scene, /wifi, /update, rename).</description>
<parameter name="activeForm">Writing ADR 0003

content.subject: M5.1 — App Group storage with migration
content.description:
Add the app group entitlement to the app target and the widget extension. Move KnownRobots off UserDefaults.standard onto the shared suite (KnownRobot already takes a UserDefaults through its initialiser). Migrate existing entries on first run so a user's known robots are not lost on update.</description>
<parameter name="activeForm">Wiring the App Group

content.subject: M5.2 — robot snapshot the widget can read
content.description:
A widget extension lives for seconds and cannot hold the state WebSocket or a WebRTC session, so it renders a snapshot the app writes into the App Group: robot name, awake/asleep, running app, and the time it was taken. Staleness must be explicit — a widget confidently showing "awake" for a robot that is off is worse than one saying it has no fresh data.</description>
<parameter name="activeForm">Building the widget snapshot

content.subject: M5.3 — widget extension and deep links
content.description:
New iOS-only widget extension target in Apps/Project.swift (no macOS per the user's decision), timeline provider over the snapshot, small and medium families. Tapping opens the right tab, which needs onOpenURL handling in ReachyRootView — none exists yet.</description>
<parameter name="activeForm">Building the widget extension

content.subject: M5.4 — App Intents over the local network
content.description:
Wake, sleep and start-app intents that reach the robot over plain HTTP on the LAN. Remote actions through the relay are explicitly out of scope (user's decision): a WebRTC session cannot be negotiated inside an intent's deadline. Out of network the intent must fail with something a user can act on. Local Network permission in an extension is its own process and must be verified on device, not assumed.</description>
<parameter name="activeForm">Building the App Intents

content.subject: M5.5 — previews and recorded references for the widget
content.description:
Project rule 8: every state a user can land in gets a preview and a recorded reference — no robot known, asleep, awake, running an app, and stale data. Widget views render through WidgetKit, so check how they fit the existing Prefire pipeline before assuming they do.</description>

content.subject: ADR 0003 — remote access over the Hugging Face relay
content.description:
Record the decisions already shipped and verified: HF as this app's own account (public OAuth client + PKCE, token in Keychain, live sign-in confirmed on device), the central relay as SSE + POST, the WebRTC data channel as the remote control surface, reply correlation on a wire with no request ids, assembled DaemonStatus, and what the remote path deliberately cannot do (3D scene, /wifi, /update, rename).</description>
<parameter name="activeForm">Writing ADR 0003

content.subject: M5.1 — App Group storage with migration
content.description:
Add the app group entitlement to the app target and the widget extension. Move KnownRobots off UserDefaults.standard onto the shared suite (KnownRobot already takes a UserDefaults through its initialiser). Migrate existing entries on first run so a user's known robots are not lost on update.</description>
<parameter name="activeForm">Wiring the App Group

content.subject: M5.2 — robot snapshot the widget can read
content.description:
A widget extension lives for seconds and cannot hold the state WebSocket or a WebRTC session, so it renders a snapshot the app writes into the App Group: robot name, awake/asleep, running app, and the time it was taken. Staleness must be explicit — a widget confidently showing "awake" for a robot that is off is worse than one saying it has no fresh data.</description>
<parameter name="activeForm">Building the widget snapshot

content.subject: M5.3 — widget extension and deep links
content.description:
New iOS-only widget extension target in Apps/Project.swift (no macOS per the user's decision), timeline provider over the snapshot, small and medium families. Tapping opens the right tab, which needs onOpenURL handling in ReachyRootView — none exists yet.</description>
<parameter name="activeForm">Building the widget extension

content.subject: M5.4 — App Intents over the local network
content.description:
Wake, sleep and start-app intents that reach the robot over plain HTTP on the LAN. Remote actions through the relay are explicitly out of scope (user's decision): a WebRTC session cannot be negotiated inside an intent's deadline. Out of network the intent must fail with something a user can act on. Local Network permission in an extension is its own process and must be verified on device, not assumed.</description>
<parameter name="activeForm">Building the App Intents

content.subject: M5.5 — previews and recorded references for the widget
content.description:
Project rule 8: every state a user can land in gets a preview and a recorded reference — no robot known, asleep, awake, running an app, and stale data. Widget views render through WidgetKit, so check how they fit the existing Prefire pipeline before assuming they do.</description>

Record the decisions already shipped and verified: HF as this app's own account (public OAuth client + PKCE, token in Keychain, live sign-in confirmed on device), the central relay as SSE + POST, the WebRTC data channel as the remote control surface, reply correlation on a wire with no request ids, assembled DaemonStatus, and what the remote path deliberately cannot do (3D scene, /wifi, /update, rename).</description>

content.subject: M5.1 — App Group storage with migration
content.description:
Add the app group entitlement to the app target and the widget extension. Move KnownRobots off UserDefaults.standard onto the shared suite (KnownRobot already takes a UserDefaults through its initialiser). Migrate existing entries on first run so a user's known robots are not lost on update.</description>
<parameter name="activeForm">Wiring the App Group

content.subject: M5.2 — robot snapshot the widget can read
content.description:
A widget extension lives for seconds and cannot hold the state WebSocket or a WebRTC session, so it renders a snapshot the app writes into the App Group: robot name, awake/asleep, running app, and the time it was taken. Staleness must be explicit — a widget confidently showing "awake" for a robot that is off is worse than one saying it has no fresh data.</description>

content.subject: M5.3 — widget extension and deep links
content.description:
New iOS-only widget extension target in Apps/Project.swift (no macOS per the user's decision), timeline provider over the snapshot, small and medium families. Tapping opens the right tab, which needs onOpenURL handling in ReachyRootView — none exists yet.</description>
<parameter name="activeForm">Building the widget extension

content.subject: M5.4 — App Intents over the local network
content.description:
Wake, sleep and start-app intents that reach the robot over plain HTTP on the LAN. Remote actions through the relay are explicitly out of scope (user's decision): a WebRTC session cannot be negotiated inside an intent's deadline. Out of network the intent must fail with something a user can act on. Local Network permission in an extension is its own process and must be verified on device, not assumed.</description>

The churn note claims fourteen previews and roughly twenty unrelated references move deterministically each run, but my observations this session show only eight previews in M9.

The HF sign-in screen added one preview with zero shifts, and the widget added six previews with zero shifts. So there's no mass churn happening here. The key insight is that shifts come from previews with indeterminate ProgressView spinners, not from the number of previews themselves—adding six previews without spinners caused no movement, and even the spinner preview didn't shift other tests. The effect scales with spinner count, not preview count overall. This is the honest clarification based on what I'm seeing.

Now I'm diving into the central relay protocol research—endpoints, message types, peer roles, eviction logic, and reason codes—pulling facts from the CentralRelayClient code and the sim daemon logs. # The Hugging Face central relay

How a robot on someone else's network becomes reachable, and what the relay does and does not carry. Written against
the daemon's own client (`.venv-sim/lib/python3.12/site-packages/reachy_mini/media/central_signaling_relay.py`) and
this app's `Sources/ReachyKit/Central/`. Specification, never code to port (rule 1).

Decisions taken on top of this live in [ADR 0003](../adr/0003-remote-access-over-the-hugging-face-relay.md).

## What it is

A Hugging Face Space — `https://pollen-robotics-reachy-mini-central.hf.space`, overridable through
`REACHY_CENTRAL_URL` on the robot and `CentralRelayClient.Configuration.baseURL` here. Both ends authenticate with a
Hugging Face token, and central only ever introduces two peers that presented one for the same account.

It is a **signalling broker, not a tunnel.** Once the WebRTC session is up, video, audio and the data channel flow
peer-to-peer; central sees none of it. The daemon's HTTP port is never exposed, which is why remote access does not
weaken ADR 0001's position.

## Routes

Everything is HTTP with `Authorization: Bearer <hf-token>`.

| Route                    | Shape                                                                                      |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `GET /events`            | Server-sent events, one JSON message per `data:` line. The inbound half of signalling.      |
| `POST /send`             | One JSON message. The outbound half; some messages answer synchronously in the response.    |
| `GET /api/robot-status`  | `{robots: [...]}` — the account's robots as central currently sees them.                    |
| `GET /health`            | Unauthenticated liveness.                                                                   |

## Message vocabulary

Modelled in `Sources/ReachyKit/Transport/SignalingMessage.swift`, shared with the LAN path — the robot's own
`webrtcsink` signalling server speaks the same dialect on port 8443, which is why one transport seam serves both.

- `welcome(peerID)` — first frame on `/events`; the id central knows this client by.
- `setPeerStatus(roles, name)` — how a peer announces itself. `["listener"]` for this app, `["producer"]` for a robot.
  The `name` is what the robot's owner sees holding their robot.
- `list` → `producerList([Producer])` — robots available to this token.
- `startSession(peerID)` → `sessionStarted(peerID, sessionID)`, or a rejection.
- `sdp(sessionID, type, sdp)` and `ice(sessionID, candidate, …)` — the negotiation itself.
- `endSession(sessionID, reason)` — either side.

## Things that cost time to find out

- **Announce before reporting a connection.** Central evicts peers with no recent inbound traffic, and the robot's own
  relay registers as a producer before flipping its state to connected. A listener that reports itself connected
  before sending `setPeerStatus` is visible to nothing.
- **Presence in the listing _is_ the online signal.** Central sweeps a peer whose lease lapsed, so a robot that is off
  is absent rather than listed as offline. The UI shows an empty list, never a greyed-out robot.
- **Rejections carry short reason codes**, and they mean genuinely different things — `robot_busy` (something is
  running on it, worth retrying), `local_app_started` (somebody walked up to the robot; retrying takes it from them),
  `install_id_takeover` (the same account opened it elsewhere; retrying starts a bouncing match). Modelled in
  `RemoteSessionEnd`, which also carries an unknown code through verbatim so a bug report can name it.
- **1200 requests a minute per token.** Retrying through a `429` turns a limit into a ban, so `rateLimited` is its own
  failure rather than another `http(Int)`.
- **60 s of silence ends the stream.** Central keepalives well inside that; `readTimeout` matches the robot's budget.
- **`unauthorized` is not worth retrying** — the same token will be refused again. It is the signal to ask for a fresh
  sign-in, which is what `YourReachiesModel.needsSignIn` renders.

## What cannot be tested here

`sim-daemon` cannot stand in for central: it has no token, registers no producer, and `test:sim` therefore never
exercises any of this. Both ends are unit-tested against stubs — `CentralRelayClient` and `CentralSignalingTransport`
over `StubURLProtocol` — but the joint needs a live `RTCDataChannel`, which does not exist outside a real peer
connection. That part is verified by hand, on hardware.

- `setPeerStatus(roles, name)` — how a peer announces itself. `["listener"]` for this app, `["producer"]` for a robot.
  The `name` is what the robot's owner sees holding their robot.
- `list` → `producerList([Producer])` — robots available to this token.
- `startSession(peerID)` → `sessionStarted(peerID, sessionID)`, or a rejection.
- `sdp(sessionID, type, sdp)` and `ice(sessionID, candidate, …)` — the negotiation itself.
- `endSession(sessionID, reason)` — either side.

## Things that cost time to find out

- **Announce before reporting a connection.** Central evicts peers with no recent inbound traffic, and the robot's own
  relay registers as a producer before flipping its state to connected. A listener that reports itself connected
  before sending `setPeerStatus` is visible to nothing.
- **Presence in the listing _is_ the online signal.** Central sweeps a peer whose lease lapsed, so a robot that is off
  is absent rather than listed as offline. The UI shows an empty list, never a greyed-out robot.
- **Rejections carry short reason codes**, and they mean genuinely different things — `robot_busy` (something is
  running on it, worth retrying), `local_app_started` (somebody walked up to the robot; retrying takes it from them),
  `install_id_takeover` (the same account opened it elsewhere; retrying starts a bouncing match). Modelled in
  `RemoteSessionEnd`, which also carries an unknown code through verbatim so a bug report can name it.
- **1200 requests a minute per token.** Retrying through a `429` turns a limit into a ban, so `rateLimited` is its own
  failure rather than another `http(Int)`.
- **60 s of silence ends the stream.** Central keepalives well inside that; `readTimeout` matches the robot's budget.
- **`unauthorized` is not worth retrying** — the same token will be refused again. It is the signal to ask for a fresh
  sign-in, which is what `YourReachiesModel.needsSignIn` renders.

## What cannot be tested here

`sim-daemon` cannot stand in for central: it has no token, registers no producer, and `test:sim` therefore never
exercises any of this. Both ends are unit-tested against stubs — `CentralRelayClient` and `CentralSignalingTransport`
over `StubURLProtocol` — but the joint needs a live `RTCDataChannel`, which does not exist outside a real peer
connection. That part is verified by hand, on hardware.

## Routes

Everything is HTTP with `Authorization: Bearer <hf-token>`.

| Route                   | Shape                                                                                    |
| ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `GET /events`           | Server-sent events, one JSON message per `data:` line. The inbound half of signalling.   |
| `POST /send`            | One JSON message. The outbound half; some messages answer synchronously in the response. |
| `GET /api/robot-status` | `{robots: [...]}` — the account's robots as central currently sees them.                 |
| `GET /health`           | Unauthenticated liveness.                                                                |

## Message vocabulary

Modelled in `Sources/ReachyKit/Transport/SignalingMessage.swift`, shared with the LAN path — the robot's own
`webrtcsink` signalling server speaks the same dialect on port 8443, which is why one transport seam serves both.

- `welcome(peerID)` — first frame on `/events`; the id central knows this client by.
- `setPeerStatus(roles, name)` — how a peer announces itself. `["listener"]` for this app, `["producer"]` for a robot.
  The `name` is what the robot's owner sees holding their robot.
- `list` → `producerList([Producer])` — robots available to this token.
- `startSession(peerID)` → `sessionStarted(peerID, sessionID)`, or a rejection.
- `sdp(sessionID, type, sdp)` and `ice(sessionID, candidate, …)` — the negotiation itself.
- `endSession(sessionID, reason)` — either side.

## Things that cost time to find out

- **Announce before reporting a connection.** Central evicts peers with no recent inbound traffic, and the robot's own
  relay registers as a producer before flipping its state to connected. A listener that reports itself connected
  before sending `setPeerStatus` is visible to nothing.
- **Presence in the listing _is_ the online signal.** Central sweeps a peer whose lease lapsed, so a robot that is off
  is absent rather than listed as offline. The UI shows an empty list, never a greyed-out robot.
- **Rejections carry short reason codes**, and they mean genuinely different things — `robot_busy` (something is
  running on it, worth retrying), `local_app_started` (somebody walked up to the robot; retrying takes it from them),
  `install_id_takeover` (the same account opened it elsewhere; retrying starts a bouncing match). Modelled in
  `RemoteSessionEnd`, which also carries an unknown code through verbatim so a bug report can name it.
- **1200 requests a minute per token.** Retrying through a `429` turns a limit into a ban, so `rateLimited` is its own
  failure rather than another `http(Int)`.
- **60 s of silence ends the stream.** Central keepalives well inside that; `readTimeout` matches the robot's budget.
- **`unauthorized` is not worth retrying** — the same token will be refused again. It is the signal to ask for a fresh
  sign-in, which is what `YourReachiesModel.needsSignIn` renders.

## What cannot be tested here

`sim-daemon` cannot stand in for central: it has no token, registers no producer, and `test:sim` therefore never
exercises any of this. Both ends are unit-tested against stubs — `CentralRelayClient` and `CentralSignalingTransport`
over `StubURLProtocol` — but the joint needs a live `RTCDataChannel`, which does not exist outside a real peer
connection. That part is verified by hand, on hardware.

Всё доделано, дерево чистое.

## Что вошло в M10 (`a3dd1e3`)

**`docs/research/central-relay.md`** — протокол, вычитанный из клиента демона и нашего: маршруты (`/events`, `/send`, `/api/robot-status`, `/health`), словарь сообщений, общий с LAN-сигналингом, и то, что стоило времени — анонс до объявления соединения, присутствие в списке *как* сигнал онлайна, различие кодов отказа, лимит 1200 запросов в минуту.

**`.claude/rules/daemon-api.md`** — поверхность `/api/hf-auth/*` робота, включая ту находку, что определила дизайн входа: **ни один маршрут не отдаёт токен**, поэтому делегировать авторизацию роботу и забрать токен себе невозможно.

**Заметка про churn эталонов исправлена.** Она утверждала пропорцию, которой нет: «четырнадцать превью → двадцать чужих эталонов». За эту сессию три добавления — восемь превью, потом одно, потом шесть, причём одно со спиннером — не сдвинули ни одного. Переписал честно: двигает не факт добавления превью, а сдвиг тайминга прогона, поэтому широкий сдвиг нужно объяснять, а не ожидать.

Сирота `ReachySpike.entitlements` удалена.

## Весь план закрыт

Все десять вех: магазин приложений, вход в Hugging Face, удалённый доступ, «Your Reachies», виджеты с Control Center, документация. Каждая ветка смержена в main, worktree убраны.

## Что остаётся непроверенным — прямо, без смягчений

Это не следствие невыполненной работы, а граница того, что можно проверить без железа и без ручных действий:

- **Виджет не размещён.** Приложение с расширением стоит на iPhone, но добавить виджет на экран и кнопки в Пункт управления могу только вы. Ключевая проверка — оставить телефон и убедиться, что через полчаса виджет сам перешёл на «Last seen …» вместо «Awake».
- **Local Network permission у расширения.** Отдельный процесс, отдельное разрешение; интенты идут по локальной сети, и как это поведёт себя из расширения — покажет только запуск.
- **Полная удалённая цепочка на живом роботе.** Оба конца покрыты тестами, стык через настоящий `RTCDataChannel` непроверяем в CI — у `ReachyMedia` нет тестового таргета. Вход через OAuth вы подтвердили, но сессию к роботу через релей — ещё нет.
- **`test:sim` даёт 6 из 7.** WebRTC-тест падает из-за сломанного GStreamer в `.venv-sim` (Opus-кодек), а не из-за кода — доказано по времени в логе. Чинится пересозданием окружения, если понадобится.
